articles.title: Norway's King Harald dies aged 89: A beloved monarch buffeted by family crises
articles.summary: The late king, who reigned for 35 years, broke with tradition by marrying a commoner and was widely loved by Norwegians.

blocks.text: Harald was born on 21 February 1937 on the Skaugum estate near Oslo. He was three when dictator Adolf Hitler ordered Norway's invasion by Nazi Germany early in World War Two.
Harald's mother fled with her children across the border to Sweden, and they travelled to the US on the invitation of President Franklin D Roosevelt.

Prince Harald returned with his family to Norway at the end of the war and completed his school and compulsory military service. He became crown prince in 1957, and studied social science, history and economics at Balliol College in Oxford from 1960 to 1962.

He met Sonja Haraldsen, a non-royal and the daughter of a businessman, at a party, but the crown prince had to wait nine years before he was allowed to marry her. Eventually he told his father that if he could not marry Sonja, he would stay single, King Harald told Norway's public broadcaster, external.
His father finally gave his consent, and the couple wed in Oslo Cathedral on 29 August 1968.
Harald's choice paved the way for his own two children to marry commoners too, and for Vagle, that "helped bring an end to a very male-dominated Royal Family".
When his father became ill in 1990, the crown prince became regent. Harald then ascended to the throne when Olav died on 17 January 1991.
The new king came into his own around 2000, according to historian Trond Norén Isaksen, growing from a shy man into someone much more open and empathetic.

In July 2011 Harald faced his greatest challenge yet as king, when neo-Nazi Anders Breivik murdered eight people with a car bomb in Oslo before moving on to a youth camp on the island of Utøya, where he shot dead 69 others, most of them teenagers.

He gave a televised address the next day, and weeks later he delivered a speech, empathising with the victims and their families as a father, grandfather, husband, and king. On the verge of tears, his voice quivered and broke.
"I can only imagine the depth of your pain. As King of this nation, I feel for each and every one of you," he said.
Looking back, historian Ole-Jørgen Schulsrud-Hansen said: "I think that moment has been burned into our minds of what a monarchy should be."
In 2016, the king made headlines again by giving a, external speech , externalsupporting diversity of religion, ethnicity and sexual orientation.

He said Norwegians are from "Afghanistan, Pakistan and Poland, from Sweden, Somalia, and Syria," they "believe in God, Allah, the Universe and nothing", and they "are girls who love girls, boys who love boys, and girls and boys who love each other".

When Crown Prince Haakon married Mette-Marit in 2001, the king and queen welcomed her four-year-old son from a previous relationship. Høiby was treated as one of the family, but the royal house later stressed he was never a royal.

The king's daughter Princess Märtha Louise initially married a Norwegian writer before controversially remarrying in 2024 to an American self-styled shaman. The couple's business activities eventually led to her halting her royal duties.

While some Norwegians may have felt Harald was too lenient with his family's controversial life decisions, Vagle believes he had "shown himself to be someone who puts talking things through ahead of issuing harsh instructions".
As the king's health declined, he permanently reduced his public engagements in April 2024.

More recently he was treated with cortisone for a rare blood condition, haemolytic anaemia, which causes the number of red blood cells in the body to be reduced. He entered hospital on 17 August and his son became regent, taking over his activities.
This year alone the Norwegian royal family has faced compounded personal health challenges and scandals.

The rape trial of Høiby, convicted of multiple offences in June, hung over the royal family for many months. He has now appealed against a four-year jail term and appeared at Harald's bedside shortly before he died.
Days before the trial began, documents were released revealing his mother Mette-Marit's frequent contact with Epstein.
She later apologised to King Harald and Queen Sonja for her three-year friendship with Epstein and admitted to "poor judgement".
Two days after her son's trial came to an end, Mette-Marit received a lung transplant. She had been diagnosed with a rare form of pulmonary fibrosis eight years earlier.
Her doctors will not declare her stable until a year after the transplant, and King Haakon will face a difficult period of succession as he continues to support her.
The crises surrounding the monarchy have had an effect on its popularity. One poll for Aftenposten newspaper found that support had dropped from 72% in 2024 to 54%.
Other polls suggested almost half of Norwegians believed Mette-Marit could no longer become queen, although Haakon is now highly likely to say she will.
However, Vagle said criticism was rarely directed at the late king personally, leaving her with the impression that "everyone has loved King Harald".
"When things go wrong in the royal family, people tend to blame anyone but the king," Isaksen remarked.

Haakon has faced questions about the turbulence surrounding his own household that will "follow him into his position as a king", according to Taalesen, however she believes he has shown leadership and dealt with recent events well.
The royal family's main strategy has been to separate itself from Høiby's trial, and Schulsrud-Hansen believes that has largely succeeded.
Although there may be further scrutiny over the Epstein files, the focus for Norwegians now will be on remembering a "greatly beloved king" and supporting his son.

articles.title: Public spaces now double as flood‑control facilities in QC
articles.summary: Quezon City is using two public spaces as flood-control facilities capable of collectively storing approximately 14,169.5 cubic meters of rainwater to help reduce flooding during the rainy season.…

blocks.text: The newly opened multi-purpose open field at the Quezon Memorial Circle (QMC), which serves as a venue for sports, leisure, and community activities. (Photo courtesy of the Quezon City government)
Quezon City is using two public spaces as flood-control facilities capable of collectively storing approximately 14,169.5 cubic meters of rainwater to help reduce flooding during the rainy season.
The capacity comes from the newly inaugurated Quezon Memorial Circle (QMC) Open Field and the lagoon within the Quezon City Hall complex.
The 12,000-square-meter QMC Open Field features a retention pond, detention tank, and basin designed to collect excess floodwater from the park and portions of the adjacent Elliptical Road.

These facilities can store up to 1,119.5 cubic meters of water, equivalent to approximately 5,597 commonly used blue drums, helping reduce the volume and speed of stormwater flowing into surrounding drainage systems.
The open field also has a wide green area that allows rainwater to be absorbed naturally into the ground.

Mayor Joy Belmonte said the projects are part of the city’s continuing investment in the QC Drainage Master Plan to protect residents and businesses, reduce flooding, and make the city safer and more climate-resilient.

“Flood control is not only about building bigger and harder infrastructure. It is also about creating more spaces that can hold, absorb, and manage water before it overwhelms our communities,” Belmonte said.

The city government is also using the lagoon within the City Hall complex as a retention pond that can store approximately 13,050 cubic meters of rainwater, equivalent to more than five Olympic-sized swimming pools.
The collected and filtered rainwater is reused for the city’s greening initiatives and toilet flushing in city-owned facilities, helping conserve potable water while reducing runoff.

During recent periods of heavy rain, the city government observed reduced flooding along portions of the Elliptical Road, where the QMC retention pond helped manage and temporarily store excess stormwater.
The QMC Open Field and City Hall lagoon demonstrate how public spaces can serve both flood-control and recreational purposes while helping manage excess rainwater.

articles.title: Gov’t lets firms defer tax perks amid fuel crisis
articles.summary: The government has allowed companies registered with investment promotion agencies (IPAs) to temporarily defer their tax incentives in a bid to help them recover from the impact of the ongoing fuel…

blocks.text: The government has allowed companies registered with investment promotion agencies (IPAs) to temporarily defer their tax incentives in a bid to help them recover from the impact of the ongoing fuel crisis.

In Resolution No. 011-2026 dated May 18 but only made public on Aug. 26, the Cabinet-level interagency Fiscal Incentives Review Board (FIRB) authorized IPAs to adopt the measure in support of affected registered business enterprises (RBEs).
Under the policy, RBEs may apply to their respective IPAs to defer their entitlement to the income tax holiday (ITH), special corporate income tax (SCIT), or enhanced deductions regime.
The period of deferment will correspond to the extent to which an RBE’s operations have been affected or disrupted by the fuel crisis caused by the war in the Middle East, according to FIRB.
Once granted, the RBE shall pay the income tax due for the taxable year covered by the deferred period.
FIRB is also allowing RBEs to postpone the start of commercial operations of their projects while preserving their full entitlement to approved incentives.
FIRB said these measures aim to ensure “business continuity, sustain investments, protect employment, and preserve the country’s competitiveness as an investment destination.”
Since the war in the Middle East broke out in February, FIRB noted that higher fuel prices have been disrupting logistics and supply chains, heightening operational costs for RBEs.
On top of this, exporting RBEs are also being confronted with the war’s direct and indirect impact on trade flows. Meanwhile, RBEs serving the domestic market are facing weaker demand amid inflation.

Through the deferment of incentives, the government seeks to prevent companies from essentially losing the value of their time-limited tax incentives during a period when they may be earning little taxable income.

Under the Corporate Recovery and Tax Incentives for Enterprises to Maximize Opportunities for Reinvigorating the Economy (CREATE MORE) Act, incentives such as the ITH are granted for a certain number of years from the start of commercial operations.
RBEs register their projects or activities with IPAs to qualify for fiscal and non-fiscal incentives aimed at supporting their operations and encouraging investments.
FIRB said the temporary deferment measures took effect on March 24 and shall remain in force for one year, unless Executive Order (EO) No. 110 is lifted or extended.
President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. issued EO 110 to declare the Philippines under a state of national energy emergency due to the war in the Middle East and its threat to the country’s energy supply.

The FIRB resolution was signed by then Acting Department of Budget and Management (DBM) Secretary Rolando U. Toledo, Department of Economy, Planning, and Development (DEPDev) Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan, Acting Executive Secretary Ralph G. Recto, FIRB Co-Chairperson and Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) Secretary Ma. Cristina A. Roque, and FIRB Chairperson and Department of Finance (DOF) Secretary Frederick D. Go.

FIRB earlier approved the expansion of the work-from-home (WFH) policy to 90 percent of the workforce from the previous 50 percent to help RBEs ease the burden of higher fuel costs on their employees.

articles.title: FACT CHECK: Photo of Alex Eala carrying Sara Duterte-themed bag is AI-generated
articles.summary: A reverse image search reveals that professional tennis player Alex Eala was actually carrying a bag from a well-known brand that she represents as a global ambassador

blocks.text: Claim: Filipina tennis player Alex Eala was photographed carrying a bag featuring the name and face of Vice President Sara Duterte.
Why we fact-checked this: A Facebook user posted the claim on the page “Protect Vice President Sara Duterte,” which currently has 205,000 members.
The image of Eala, posted on August 20, shows a green bag with Duterte’s face alongside the year “2028.” As of writing, the post has garnered 1,000 reactions, 208 comments, and 127 shares.

Some social media users believed that Eala was supporting Duterte’s 2028 presidential bid. One user even commented, “Galing naman keep it up carry on Alex Solid Duterte,” while others claimed that green — Duterte’s official campaign color in the 2022 elections — is the tennis player’s lucky color.
The facts: The photo is edited. A reverse Google image search reveals that Eala was actually carrying a bag from a well-known sports brand that she represents as a global ambassador.

The unaltered photo of Eala, showing her ahead of her Mubadala DC Open Finals match against world No. 3 Jessica Pegula of the United States, was published across various social media accounts, including by sports journalist Dyan Castillejo. Additional photos with different angles from the same event posted by the Rafa Nadal Academy confirm that the bag in the misleading post had been edited.

Furthermore, AI detection tool Sightengine indicated a 99% probability that the photo is AI-generated or manipulated. Other detection tools, including ZeroGPT and DeepAI, yielded similar results with a 94% probability.

The edited photo, which was shared on a Duterte supporters’ group, appears to be a show of support for the Vice President amid her ongoing impeachment trial and her declared bid for the presidency in 2028 — hence the “2028” in the bag’s design.

Disinformation target: Eala holds the record as the highest-ranked Filipina in tennis history, reaching world No. 18 in the Women’s Tennis Association rankings as of August 2026. The young tennis star dominated news headlines after winning her first-ever WTA Tour crown in the Washington Open.

Eala’s widespread fame has made her a target for false claims. Rappler previously debunked a fake quote card in which Eala allegedly made a statement denying political meaning to her choice of attire. Rappler has also previously debunked other posts featuring AI-generated photos of Eala. – Lyndee Buenagua/Rappler.com
Lyndee Buenagua is journalist based in Bicol and Baguio, and an alumna of Aries Rufo Journalism Fellowship of Rappler for 2024.

Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

articles.title: Remula: DILG 'very serious' in protecting female cops
articles.summary: Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) Secretary Jonvic Remulla has declared that the agency is "very serious" when it comes to protecting female police officers from gender-based…

blocks.text: Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) Secretary Jonvic Remulla has declared that the agency is "very serious" when it comes to protecting female police officers from gender-based violence.
Remulla affirmed this commitment during the agency's marathon budget hearing Thursday, Aug. 27 before the House Committee on Appropriations.
Gabriela Party-list Rep. Sarah Elago raised the issue on violence against women and children (VAWC) in the Philippine National Police (PNP) during the budget deliberations.
“We take it very seriously, ma’am, that if there is harassment among the ranks, that we will file the appropriate charges, whoever they may be,” Remulla told the Makabayan lawmaker.

“In fact, maybe a member of Congress was also charged by the PNP for violence against women among his security personnel and the charges have been filed by the DOJ (Department of Justice),” he added, referring to a case involving Marikina 1st district Rep. Marcy Teodoro.
"I take it very seriously and I prosecute it to the best of my ability," Remulla added, referring to such cases in general.
Remulla is concurrently the chairman of National Police Commission (Napolcom), which supervises the PNP.
Elago also urged the DILG to amend its policy on settlement or reconciliation between perpetrators and victims, citing it is against the VAWC law.

“Dapat niyo pong baguhin itong policy na ito kasi sa ilalim po ng anti-VAWC law, bawal po ang pagaareglo lalong lalo na po sa mga kaso ng physical abuse—hindi po dapat ito pinapayagan,” said the congresswoman from the Makabayan bloc.
(You need to change this policy because under the Anti-VAWC law, settlements are prohibited, especially in cases of physical abuse—this should not be allowed.)
Remulla reassured Elago that the DILG will comply and make the necessary adjustments.

“I particularly am very sensitive about this. If there is any complaint against harassment of women personnel in the PNP, I take it very seriously and [I’ll] prosecute [the perpetrators] to the best of my ability,” Remulla said.
Teodoro has repeatedly denied the allegations against him.

articles.title: ‘We execute the prick’: Charles Perrottet sent text plotting downfall of NSW Liberal minister, Icac hears
articles.summary: Brother of former state premier tells Icac he sent message to his wife referring to a plan to damage the career of rival David Elliott

blocks.text: Charles Perrottet wrote about a plan to damage a Liberal minister’s career after his brother Dominic’s accession to the New South Wales premiership in October 2021, stating “we execute the prick once party room is over”, a corruption inquiry has heard.

The younger brother of the former premier told the Independent Commission Against Corruption (Icac) on Friday a message he sent to his wife two days before Dominic Perrottet was elected premier by Liberal MPs referred to a plan to oust the former Liberal police minister David Elliott.

As part of its inquiry into alleged corruption by people associated with the NSW Liberals, Icac is investigating whether between 2020 and 2023, figures including Charles Perrottet took prohibited political donations from fugitive property developer Jean Nassif and his company Toplace, including for outcomes such as damaging the career of Elliott.
Dominic Perrottet is not named as a person of interest in Icac’s investigation and is not accused of any wrongdoing.
Charles Perrottet appeared at the inquiry immediately after his wife, Anita Perrottet, on Friday.

During Anita Perrottet’s evidence, counsel assisting Dr Peggy Dwyer SC read out text messages between the couple from Sunday 3 October 2021, two days before a party room vote that elected Dominic Perrottet, a member of the Liberals’ conservative right faction, as premier under an agreement brokered with the moderate faction headed by Matt Kean that weekend.
Charles Perrottet wrote that he “had a long call with Dom”.
“He [Dominic Perrottet] thanked me for everything, not just this weekend, but the last 20 years to get here. Apologised for the Elliott stuff.”
In a subsequent message, Anita Perrottet wrote: “Did Dom confirm that he isn’t going to give Elliott a ministry?”

“I didn’t ask,” Charles Perrottet wrote back. “That’s a call for tomorrow. I told him to turn his phone off and savour the moment with Helen, as tomorrow and Tuesday is going to be crucial in showing unity. We execute the prick as soon as party room is over.”

At the end of his evidence on Friday, Charles Perrottet accepted that the message referred to Elliott, but told the inquiry he was annoyed because Elliott had been running an “anyone but Dom” campaign among MPs.
“I was pretty annoyed at the time of the way David handled himself over the course of the weekend,” he said.

Under repeated questioning from Dwyer and presiding commissioner Fabian Gleeson, Anita Perrottet said she could not recall the messages. She repeatedly rejected the suggestion that her husband was the “muscle” in the Liberal conservative right faction or a “power broker” in the party.

Elliott, who was the police minister in the Berejiklian government, was subsequently moved to the transport portfolio in a reshuffle. Last week, Elliott told the inquiry he was targeted by Nassif due to his opposition to Toplace developments.

The inquiry has previously heard legally intercepted phone calls featuring Nassif in which he claimed he had “forced the boys” to get rid of Elliott’s seat of Baulkham Hills, and had sent “Castle Hill fucking hundreds of new members”. Elliott retired from politics before the March 2023 election after his seat was abolished and he could not find sufficient support from branches in Castle Hill.

Charles Perrottet, and Liberal operatives Christian Ellis and Jeremy Greenwood, allegedly anticipated receiving $2m to be distributed evenly between them from Nassif. The commission has heard Anita Perrottet allegedly received Charles’s share through invoices from her business Macquarie Consulting to lobbying companies Beckington, controlled by Ellis and Greenwood, and JPG Advisory, controlled by Greenwood.

On Friday, Charles Perrottet told the inquiry he began to provide advice to Nassif on his developments through Beckington, after being introduced to him by Greenwood in late 2019 or early 2020. He said he and Nassif met face-to-face 10 to 12 times.

Asked if Greenwood suggested he “share in the financial spoils” of the advice, Charles Perrottet, who already had a paid job at BP, told the hearing they agreed to an arrangement under which Anita would be compensated.
after newsletter promotion
“I think the words to the effect were, ‘You’ve got a commercial relationship with Anita. She’s enjoying coming back to work. Just continue that relationship and look after her.’”
Charles Perrottet told the inquiry he would tell Nassif “what he wanted to hear,” and that Nassif was aware he was a member of the conservative right faction.
“Predominantly, he would complain about what he saw was unfair treatment for his projects. He’d complain about individuals,” Charles Perrottet said.

“He was very unhappy with David Elliott. I would tell him that there were plans like that [to get rid of David Elliott]. I was supportive of that position, but that was very different to what was actually occurring within the party.”

Charles Perrottet said it was “not accurate” to say his and Nassif’s goals aligned, but admitted to a longstanding feud with Elliott’s centre-right faction, following factional efforts that forced Dominic Perrottet to move from the seat of Castle Hill to Hawkesbury at the 2015 election.
“If they’d never kicked Dom out of Castle Hill in 2015, perhaps all of them would still be in their seat,” Charles Perrottet told the inquiry on Friday.

Earlier, Anita Perrottet, who said she was not aware of Nassif at the time besides from “media reports”, was shown an email sent in October 2020 from her company account to a lobbyist sharing a “detailed summary” of one of Nassif’s developments in Rosebery in inner Sydney, mentioning Nassif and Toplace multiple times.
Dwyer asked: “You’re not prepared to admit that because you don’t want to get your husband Charles in trouble for doing work for Jean Nassif or Toplace?”
“No, it’s because I am genuinely telling the truth and trying to assist the commission,” Anita Perrottet replied.
Charles Perrottet, who has taken a leave of absence from BP during the inquiry, is expected to appear before the commission again on Monday and Tuesday next week.
On Thursday, Icac announced that Nassif, who fled Australia for Lebanon in 2022, would appear by video link. He has previously denied any wrongdoing.
The inquiry continues.

articles.title: Prosecution: Poa should explain why military certifications were used for DepEd confi funds
articles.summary: The House prosecution panel said Friday defense counsel Michael Poa has a lot to explain before the Senate impeachment court on how the P112.5 million in confidential funds of the Department of…

blocks.text: Published August 28, 2026 5:08pm
Make this your preferred source to get more updates from this publisher on Google.

The House prosecution panel said Friday defense counsel Michael Poa has a lot to explain before the Senate impeachment court on how the P112.5 million in confidential funds of the Department of Education (DepEd) was used during the tenure of Vice President Sara Duterte as Education chief.

House prosecution panel adviser and former Surigao del Norte Rep. Ace Barbers and House Deputy Speaker Paolo Ortega V of La Union cited that Poa, as then-undersecretary and spokesperson of the DepEd, already admitted before a 2024 House good government and public accountability panel that he asked certifications from military officials to justify the DepEd's confidential fund spending without informing the military officials on the purpose of such signatures.
Poa is the next witness that the prosecution will field for the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.

"What we heard from him during the Good Government [panel], we haven't heard the whole story from Atty. Michael Poa. As Assistant Chief of Staff of DepEd that time, he is in charge of a lot of documents, evaluating them, and he could be signing them. That must be made clear before the Senator-Judges," Barbers said in an online press conference.
Other Stories

"Secondly, was DepEd able to use its confidential fund properly, given that it is very rare for the DepEd to be given such a fund? Do these have a legal or illegal basis? Because if these are illegal, a lawyer such as himself should understand that these should not be allowed. You could have given a sound advice to those implementing the projects. There are many questions that need to be answered," Barbers added in a mix of English and Filipino.

Ortega, for his part, said Poa's resignation as a DepEd official in July 2024 amid the controversy on DepEd's confidential fund spending is something that should be addressed before the impeachment court.

"During the House hearings, the questions have been somehow limited since he just resigned from DepEd before he came in as resource person. The impeachment court can cover more topics that he can answer," Ortega said.

Barbers and Ortega then noted that the military certifications issued by the military officials Colonel Manaros Boransing II and Colonel Magtangol Panopio to justify DepEd's confidential fund spending, which the military officials were unaware of, carry a great weight because aside from these being public funds, it is not the job of the military to liquidate these confidential fund disbursements of DepEd.

"This organization should not interfere in politics. They should remain apolitical, they should remain neutral, and they should always be loyal to the Constitution and loyal to our Philippine flag, so it will be good for us to hear from them," Barbers said.
"Liquidating these funds is not their job. That is such a huge amount of public funds which they do not have authority to dip hands on," Barbers added. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: Philippines sees 5,486 leptospirosis cases as DOH prepares for More
articles.summary: The Department of Health (DOH) on Friday said that there have been 5,486 leptospirosis patients recorded across the Philippines from January to August 27. While the rate of cases has so far been…

blocks.text: Published August 28, 2026 5:06pm
Make this your preferred source to get more updates from this publisher on Google.
The Department of Health (DOH) on Friday said that there have been 5,486 leptospirosis patients recorded across the Philippines from January to August 27.
While the rate of cases has so far been lower compared to the same time period in the previous year, DOH officials expect the number to increase in the coming weeks.
The bacteria that causes leptospirosis has an incubation period of up to two weeks,
According to DOH Undersecretary Gloria Balboa, the current leptospirosis tally of 5,486 from January to August 27 is 23% lower than the 7,163 cases during the same time period in 2025.

However, the DOH is monitoring several regions with the highest number of leptospirosis cases. The Cordillera Administrative Region so far has the highest number of leptospirosis cases at 542, followed by Metro Manila at 521, then Central Luzon at 391 as of August 22.
Other Stories
“Binuksan na rin natin yung leptospirosis fast lane, ito po ay nandoon sa 33 DOH hospitals nandoon sa apektadong regions,” DOH Secretary Edwin Mercado said in a press conference.
(We have opened the leptospirosis fast lane in 33 DOH hospitals in the affected regions.)
Mercado said that these hospitals were in the Ilocos Region, the Cordillera Administrative Region, Cagayan Valley, Central Luzon, and the National Capital Region.
San Lazaro Hospital recently experienced a surge of leptospirosis cases, with the emergency room operating at 300% to 500% of its capacity.

The Health Secretary said that they are working to augment the manpower. Some hospitals have offered to take in mild-case patients from crowded hospitals, Balboa said, adding that they were keeping track of bed capacities across health centers.
“May sugat man o wala, at may sintomas man o wala, ay dapat po na pumunta na sa pinakamalapit na health center para maagapan at mabigyan ng tamang advice ng ating mga health workers,” Balboa said.

(Whether you have a wound or not, whether or not you have symptoms, you should go to the nearest health center to seek treatment early and be given the right advice by our health workers.) –NB, GMA News

articles.summary: The Philippine Stock Exchange index (PSEi) slid for the fourth day on Friday, Aug. 28, to end the week below the 6,000 level as MSCI rebalancing added selling pressure on investors already worried…

blocks.text: The Philippine Stock Exchange index (PSEi) slid for the fourth day on Friday, Aug. 28, to end the week below the 6,000 level as MSCI rebalancing added selling pressure on investors already worried about the impact of the previous day’s policy rate hike.
The main index dropped 48.25 points, or 0.8 percent, to close at 5,956.33. Banks led the decline, while mining and services managed to advance.
Volume surged to 2.22 billion shares worth ₱18.8 billion. Losers beat gainers—120 to 88, with 49 unchanged. Foreigners were net sellers, with net outflows of ₱3.51 billion.

“The local index closed lower with the index now below 6,000 again as intense selling pressure persisted, with the MSCI Philippine Index rebalancing influenced a significant portion of market volume. The rebalancing triggered broad-based selling across the market as investors adjusted their positions,” said Regina Capital Development Corp. managing director Luis Limlingan.
Sentiment was further weighed by the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas’ (BSP) rate hike, keeping investors cautious.
On Thursday, Aug. 27, the BSP raised its key policy rate by 25 basis points (bps) to five percent, its third rate hike this year, bringing the cumulative increase since April to 75 bps.

The central bank tightened monetary policy further as elevated inflation continued to pose risks to the economy, even as economic growth slowed to a post-pandemic low of 2.3 percent in the second quarter of 2026.

Philstocks Financial Inc. research manager Japhet Tantiangco said, “The local market extended its decline as concerns over the possible effects of the BSP’s further tightening on the local economy’s growth outlook continued to dampen sentiment.”

He added that, “The trimmed Philippine economic growth projections of Moody’s Analytics and the ASEAN+3 Macroeconomic Research Office (AMRO) also weighed on the market. Finally, the peso’s slide to a new record low added to the market’s downside.”

The Philippine peso plunged past the ₱62-per-dollar level on Friday, closing at a fresh historic low of ₱62.265 against the United States (US) dollar from the previous record of ₱61.888 just a day ago.

The local currency weakened despite the BSP’s latest rate hike—a move that typically provides support to the peso—with analysts pointing to broad US dollar strength, elevated oil prices, and heightened geopolitical uncertainty as among the factors weighing on the currency.

articles.title: PAGASA monitors 2 LPAs with potential to become tropical depressions
articles.summary: Two low-pressure areas (LPAs) are being monitored near the country, with both having a “medium chance” of developing into tropical depressions within the next 24 hours, the Philippine Atmospheric,…

blocks.text: Two low-pressure areas (LPAs) are being monitored near the country, with both having a “medium chance” of developing into tropical depressions within the next 24 hours, the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) said on Friday, Aug. 28.
The LPA designated as LPA 08i, which has been monitored since Thursday, Aug. 27, was located 560 kilometers east-northeast of Itbayat, Batanes as of 2 p.m.
LPA 08i is expected to move toward Taiwan and is not forecast to make landfall over the Philippines.
Nevertheless, PAGASA said it continues to enhance the southwest monsoon or “habagat,” which is bringing rains over parts of Luzon.
Since LPA 08i is inside the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR), it will be given the local name “Pilandok” if it develops into a tropical depression.
Meanwhile, PAGASA said a new LPA designated as LPA 08j formed outside the PAR on Friday afternoon.
It was located 1,460 kilometers east of Central Luzon as of 2 p.m.
LPA 08j may also contribute to the strengthening of the habagat in the coming days.
If LPA 08j enters the PAR and develops into a tropical depression, it will be given the local name “Queenie.”
PAGASA said the enhanced southwest monsoon is expected to bring heavy rainfall over several Luzon areas this weekend.
From Friday to Saturday noon, Aug. 29, 100 to 200 millimeters of rainfall, considered heavy to intense, may affect La Union, Benguet, Bataan, Zambales, and Occidental Mindoro.

Meanwhile, 50 to 100 millimeters of rainfall, considered moderate to heavy, may persist over Metro Manila, Ilocos Sur, Pangasinan, Abra, Tarlac, Nueva Ecija, Pampanga, Bulacan, Rizal, Cavite, Batangas, and Oriental Mindoro.
From Saturday noon to Sunday noon, Aug. 30, 100 to 200 millimeters of rainfall may continue over Ilocos Sur, La Union, Pangasinan, Benguet, Zambales, and Bataan.

Fifty to 100 millimeters of rainfall may prevail over Metro Manila, Ilocos Norte, Abra, Tarlac, Nueva Ecija, Pampanga, Bulacan, Rizal, Cavite, Laguna, Batangas, Occidental Mindoro, and Oriental Mindoro.
From Sunday noon to Monday noon, Aug. 31, 100 to 200 millimeters of rainfall may persist over Ilocos Norte, Ilocos Sur, La Union, Pangasinan, Abra, Benguet, and Zambales.

Fifty to 100 millimeters of rainfall may affect Metro Manila, Batanes, Apayao, Kalinga, Ifugao, Mountain Province, Nueva Vizcaya, Tarlac, Nueva Ecija, Bataan, Pampanga, Bulacan, Rizal, Cavite, Batangas, and Occidental Mindoro.
PAGASA advised residents in areas that may experience heavy rainfall, particularly those prone to flooding and landslides, to remain alert and continue monitoring its latest weather updates.

The Southwest Monsoon, strengthened by a low pressure area, has dumped rains across Luzon on Friday, triggering widespread flooding, especially in Pampanga and Zambales.

articles.title: King Harald V, Norway's reform-minded head of state, dead at 89
articles.summary: Norway's King ‌Harald, a ​reformer who emerged ​from the shadow ​of his well-loved ‌father over more than three decades on the ‌throne, has died aged ​89, the royal palace said on ​Friday.

blocks.text: World
Norway's King ‌Harald, a ​reformer who emerged ​from the shadow ​of his well-loved ‌father over more than three decades on the ‌throne, has died aged ​89, the royal palace said on ​Friday.
Harald was Europe's oldest living monarch

blocks.caption: Harald was taken to hospital on August 17. The palace said he was being treated for a bacterial infection in his blood. (Ritzau Scanpix/Bo Amstrup/Reuters)

blocks.text: Norway's King Harald, a reformer who emerged from the shadow of his well-loved, extrovert father over more than three decades on the throne, died on Friday at the age of 89, the royal palace said, at a time of multiple crises for the Norwegian royal family.
"King Harald passed away peacefully at Oslo University Hospital on Friday 28 August, 0635 (local time, 0435 GMT)," the royal palace said on its website.
Harald, who was Europe's oldest living monarch, was taken to hospital on August 17. The palace said he was being treated for a bacterial infection in his blood.

In 2024, he had been hospitalized for an infection while on holiday in Malaysia and received a temporary pacemaker at a hospital there. He was flown back home by the Norwegian armed forces and later fitted with a permanent device.

items: Norway crown princess's son sentenced to 4 years in prison after rape conviction

blocks.text: That same year, Harald, Norway's ceremonial head of state since 1991, said he would reduce the number of official engagements in which he took part but ruled out abdication, insisting that his oath as king was for life.

blocks.caption: People gather outside the Royal Palace Friday morning, following the death of Norway's King Harald, in Oslo. (Dylan Martinez/Reuters)

blocks.text: Harald's death comes at a tumultuous time for the royal family.

Crown Princess Mette-Marit, married to Harald's son Crown Prince Haakon, is facing intense scrutiny for her friendship with the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, a relationship for which she has apologized.

Her son Marius Hoiby, born from a relationship predating her marriage to Haakon, was found guilty in June of ​two out of four counts of rape and one count of domestic violence and sentenced to four years in prison after a seven-week trial. Both he and the prosecution have appealed the sentence.
Royal family under scrutiny
Two days after Marius was convicted, the palace said Mette-Marit had undergone a successful lung transplant, without specifying when the procedure took place.
After several weeks of recovery in hospital, she returned home and celebrated her silver wedding anniversary with Haakon in August.

Support for the monarchy dropped to 60 per cent in February 2026, from 70 per cent the previous month, according to a Norstat poll published by public broadcaster NRK, rising slightly to 64 per cent in May.
Harald had constantly remained popular with Norwegians. According to the February poll, he was the royal who best represented the Norwegian royal family, with a note of 9.2, on a scale of 1 to 10.
Descendant of Queen Victoria

A great-great-grandchild of Britain's Queen Victoria, Harald acceded to the throne in 1991 and slowly introduced modern touches that brought a ceremonial post seen mainly as a symbol of national independence into the 21st century.

blocks.caption: King Harald and Queen Sonja of Norway at the Milano Speed Skating Stadium during the Milano-Cortina 2026 Winter Olympics in Milan, Italy, in February 2026. (NTB/Heiko Junge/Reuters)

blocks.text: The popular king played a crucial role comforting the nation in times of mourning.

When far-right, anti-Islam fanatic Anders Behring Breivik killed 77 people in 2011 in Oslo and on Utoeya island, the king consoled the nation with a powerful televised speech. His voice trembling with emotion, he said that "freedom is stronger than fear."
After floods, storms and other disasters, he would travel to the scene wearing rubber boots and a well-worn jacket to meet those who had lost homes or loved ones.
Embraced openness
Late in life he spoke up for tolerance, declaring in a 2016 speech that Norwegians could have many backgrounds, beliefs and sexual orientations.
In November 2005, Harald and his wife, Sonja Haraldsen, invited 550 Norwegians to a ball to celebrate the centenary of the country's independence from Sweden.
Harald said in an interview at the time that Europe's royal families should not be tempted to reverse moves towards openness and retreat to their palace towers.
"If you've opened the gate it's very difficult to close it again," he told Reuters. "I'm not sure I'd want to close it. So far so good, as far as I'm concerned."

articles.title: House damaged after dike gives way amid heavy rains in Zambales

SAN MARCELINO, Zambales — A house was damaged after a portion of a dike gave way, sending strong floodwaters into Barangay Sta. Fe amid continuous rains brought by the southwest monsoon, or habagat.
It was fortunate that the family residing in the house was able to evacuate safely before the situation worsened, according to the local government.
The barangay hall and other structures in the area are now under water, prompting authorities and response teams to closely monitor the situation.
San Marcelino Mayor Elvis Ragadio Soria urged residents to prioritize their safety and immediately evacuate to safer areas whenever necessary.
The local government also postponed the scheduled delivery of relief packs to Barangay Sta. Fe on Friday due to the unfavorable weather.
Authorities and response teams continue to monitor developments in Sta. Fe and assess the situation as heavy rains persist in the municipality.

articles.title: Dengue outbreak declared in Bohol
articles.summary: CEBU CITY–A dengue outbreak has been declared in Bohol Province, where at least 20 deaths linked to the mosquito-borne disease have been recorded for the past weeks. With this, Bohol Gov. Erico…

blocks.text: CEBU CITY–A dengue outbreak has been declared in Bohol Province, where at least 20 deaths linked to the mosquito-borne disease have been recorded for the past weeks.

With this, Bohol Gov. Erico Aristotle Aumentado issued an Executive Order (EO), directing all local government units (LGUs) in the province to ramp up efforts to prevent the disease from spreading further .
Aumentado also ordered to strengthen the monitoring and treatment of patients.
The Bohol Provincial Health Office (BPHO) reported that as of Aug. 22, 1,883 dengue cases have been reported. The figures are seven percent higher compared to the same period last year.
Provincial officials expressed concerns over the increasing fatalities.
Dr. Fruserma Mary Uy, head of the Bohol Provincial Health Office, said that while the number of cases is almost the same as last year, the number of deaths has increased significantly.
The total number of deaths is 1.17 percent higher compared to the same period last year, exceeding the Department of Health’s acceptable level of below one percent.
“Hopefully, it won’t increase any longer,” Uy said.

In Aumentado’s EO, LGUs were ordered to intensify the implementation of the 4S strategy against dengue, reactivate their local dengue task forces and conduct community-based activities aimed at eliminating mosquito breeding areas.
Hospitals and city and municipal health offices were also directed to establish Dengue Fast Lanes to help speed up consultation and treatment.

Niel John Oclarit, development management officer IV of the Provincial Department of Health Office-Bohol, said 12 of Bohol’s 48 LGUs have exceeded the dengue epidemic threshold for three consecutive weeks.
Talibon logged the highest number of cases with 188, followed by Tagbilaran City with 172 and Ubay with 146.
Getafe recorded 108 cases, while Tubigon had 99.
Talibon also recorded the highest fatalities five followed by Tubigon with three. Getafe and Ubay each recorded two deaths.

articles.title: DepEd strengthens monitoring of textbook distribution through LRMIS
articles.summary: After completing all its target textbook procurements for 2026, the Department of Education (DepEd) is enhancing the use of its Learning Resource Management and Information System (LRMIS) to closely…

blocks.text: (MB FILE PHOTO)

After completing all its target textbook procurements for 2026, the Department of Education (DepEd) is enhancing the use of its Learning Resource Management and Information System (LRMIS) to closely monitor the distribution of textbooks and teachers’ manuals in schools.

Recently, education department secured all 105 target textbook titles for public elementary and secondary schools. It covers the successive phases of curriculum implementation from Grades 1, 4, 7, and Senior High School in 2024; Grade 3 and Grades 2, 5, and 8 in 2025; and Grades 6, 9, and 10 in 2026.

The procurement, per DepEd, resolves long-standing bottlenecks flagged by the Second Congressional Commission on Education (EDCOM II), which noted that DepEd procured only 27 of 88 required titles from 2014 to 2023.

DepEd said it will use the LRMIS to track the procurement and nationwide distribution of all 105 approved print and electronic textbook titles in real time, helping ensure that the learning materials reach schools and learners most in need.

According to DepEd Secretary Juan Edgardo Angara, the agency must now ensure that procured learning resources are tracked and accounted for throughout the distribution process and delivered to the schools, learners, and teachers that need them most.
“Natapos natin ang isang malaking bottleneck sa procurement. Pero hindi doon natatapos ang trabaho (We have resolved a major procurement bottleneck, but the work does not end there),” he said.

“Kailangan nating makita kung nasaan na ang textbooks, ilan ang hawak ng bawat school, anong grade level at learning area ang kulang, at saan puwedeng mag-reallocate kung may sobra o buffer stock. Iyan ang inaayos natin sa LRMIS (We need to determine where the textbooks are, how many each school has, which grade levels and learning areas lack materials, and where surplus or buffer stocks can be reallocated. That is what we are addressing through the LRMIS),” he added.
DepEd said achieving a one-to-one textbook-to-student ratio requires more than procuring enough textbooks.
It noted that enrollment changes every year across schools, grade levels, and localities, while textbooks may also be lost or damaged during their active use.

“Through LRMIS, schools may encode inventory data by learning resource, grade level, and learning area, which can be compared with current enrollment to identify gaps, verify deliveries, and guide the reallocation of available buffer stock,” the agency stated.

DepEd said the system offers a centralized database of learning resources, real-time inventory tracking, standardized reporting, and automated data-driven reports for schools, Schools Division Offices, Regional Offices, and the Central Office.

DepEd reported that as of Aug. 27, 37,705 public schools, or 78 percent of all schools under the department, had registered with the LRMIS, while 17,797 had recorded their textbook and teachers’ manual inventories in the system.
The latter figure accounted for about 37 percent of all DepEd schools and 77 percent of those covered by the current encoding phase, it added.
As such, the agency said schools encoded 20,520,035 learning resources in the system based on extracted regional inventory data.
Angara said encoding had been affected by bad weather in some areas, but the department remained committed to continuing the rollout without compromising school safety and operations.

“Habang mas maraming schools ang nag-e-encode, mas malinaw nating makikita kung saan kulang, saan sobra, at saan kailangang maglipat o magdagdag ng learning resources (As more schools encode their data, we will have a clearer picture of where learning resources are lacking, where there are surpluses, and where materials need to be transferred or increased),” he said.

articles.title: Teen boy allegedly messaged two others to join ‘degrading’ and ‘humiliating’ Sydney gang-rape, court hears
articles.summary:
Two 17-year-olds accused of subjecting teenage girl to hours-long sexual assault granted bail

  • Get our breaking…

blocks.text: Two boys allegedly invited to join a “degrading” and “humiliating” gang-rape in Sydney have been granted bail.
The pair are among three 17-year-olds accused of subjecting a teenage girl to an hours-long sexual assault on the night of 16 August.
The alleged instigator, a private school boy charged with 11 offences, allegedly took the girl to a football game and drinks before taking her to a home when she felt sick.
He is accused of raping her before a text message was sent to a friend, a children’s court was told on Friday.
He then invited another boy via text message to join in, with that boy attending to attack the girl, police prosecutor Sergeant Rhonda Riley alleged.
That boy has been charged with six counts of sexual assault in company as well as common assault.
The pair are alleged to have bragged about the attack to another friend, crudely telling him that he needed to have sex with the girl.
He responded to the invitation and arrived at the house and engaged in non-consensual sex with her, the court was told.
The third boy has been charged with two counts of aggravated sexual assault in company.
The alleged instigator did not apply for bail when his case was mentioned on Friday but his two co-accused did.
Children’s court judge Jeff Tunks was urged to consider that the teens had strong family supports, schooling commitments and lacked criminal histories.
Jai Rose, representing the second alleged attacker, said his client would abide by any bail conditions imposed.
Rose also pointed to the looming higher school certificate exams, prompting Sgt Riley to remark that the alleged victim would also have to complete her exams “going through fear, going through pain”.
The barrister for the third teen meanwhile suggested consent would be an issue at trial as a text after the alleged attack claimed the boy had not received necessary “context” from his co-accused.
Judge Tunks said social and sporting ties and exam delays were of little relevance to the bail assessment.
He described the alleged attack as “degrading” and a “humiliating” ordeal with “elements of menace”.
However, he granted bail to the two co-accused, finding the risks posed by the pair could be mitigated with strict conditions.
“The bail act is not used as some sort of de facto punishment for crimes that are not proven beyond reasonable doubt,” Judge Tunks said.
Both teens were ordered to be of good behaviour, report to police daily and abide by a home detention condition.
They were instructed not to contact each other or witnesses, surrender travel documents and possess only one phone.
The alleged instigator remains in juvenile detention.
He faces the most charges, including six counts of aggravated sexual assault in company and three counts of sexual intercourse without consent.
The teens’ cases return to court in October.

BAGUIO CITY – The Baguio City Police Office (BCPO) and the Cybercrime Unit are now taking appropriate action to begin the process of removing posts and videos online related to alleged incidents of violence involving students from two public high schools in the city.

BCPO City Director P Col Ruel Tagel said the move covers posts and videos circulating online that are related to the two separate incidents involving minors including an account that had posted details of some of the minors involved and appeared to be inciting violence including grave threats.

The city government and the Pinget National High School, even the Department of Education (DepEd)-Baguio had earlier appealed to the public to take down and refrain from posting and sharing the videos, as the incidents involved minors wary that continued circulation could expose the children to public shaming, harassment, insults, threats and other forms of online abuse.

Mayor Benjamin Magalong said the two cases are being handled separately, with police coordinating with concerned school authorities and social workers. The students involved have also been identified.

He encouraged the public to allow the police, school authorities and social workers to address the incidents through proper intervention while respecting the privacy, dignity and well-being of the minors involved.

articles.title: Bike patrol at Bacolod-Silay airport launched to boost security, cut fuel use
articles.summary: BACOLOD CITY - Police at the Bacolod-Silay Airport have intensified their patrol operations in and around the airport premises, following the launch of a bicycle patrol initiative aimed at…

blocks.text: The Bacolod-Silay Airport Police in Silay City, Negros Occidental, has recently launched a bike patrol initiative to strengthen police visibility in and around the airport while promoting health, fitness, and environmental sustainability. (Bacolod-Silay Airport)

BACOLOD CITY - Police at the Bacolod-Silay Airport have intensified their patrol operations in and around the airport premises, following the launch of a bicycle patrol initiative aimed at strengthening security and police visibility.

Dubbed the “Padyak ng Pulisya sa Paliparan Project” (4P’s), the initiative seeks to promote physical fitness and camaraderie among police personnel while enhancing security through mobile, foot, and bicycle patrols.

Police Major Deejay Domingo, chief of the Bacolod-Silay Airport police, said the bike patrol allows personnel to reinforce security in the area while promoting physical wellness and an eco-friendly approach to police operations.
The initiative is also expected to help reduce the unit’s fuel consumption amid ongoing tensions in the Middle East.
The program is being implemented under the supervision of Police Col. Alex Dimaculangan, chief of the Aviation Security Unit-Negros Island Region (NIR).

As part of the launching activities, police personnel also distributed rice to airport security guards through the station’s community outreach program, highlighting the unit’s commitment to public service and stronger partnerships with airport stakeholders.

The Bacolod-Silay Airport currently has 11 bicycles for the patrol initiative. Similar bike patrol operations are also being implemented in Negros Oriental, with two bicycles assigned in Dumaguete City and two in Siquijor.
Domingo said bike patrols at the airport will be conducted randomly to avoid establishing a predictable pattern and further strengthen security operations.

articles.title: PNP readies units for AI-enabled body cameras
articles.summary: The Philippine National Police (PNP) said Friday, Aug. 28, that it was gearing up for the deployment of new body-worn cameras powered by artificial intelligence (AI) that were expected to provide…

blocks.text: The Philippine National Police (PNP) said Friday, Aug. 28, that it was gearing up for the deployment of new body-worn cameras powered by artificial intelligence (AI) that were expected to provide clearer records of police encounters and operations in the field.

Police General Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr., PNP chief, said the equipment would give police officers a more reliable record of their interactions with the public while helping preserve evidence and support investigations.

“The AI-enabled body cameras will enhance the PNP’s capability to document police operations with clearer and more reliable footage. This will help preserve evidence, support investigations, and promote greater accountability among our personnel,” Nartatez said.

Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) Secretary Jonvic Remulla earlier told the House committee on appropriations during a briefing on the proposed DILG budget for 2027 that the PNP is procuring 10,000 to 20,000 new AI-enabled body-worn cameras this year.
The new cameras are expected to have better lenses and improved image quality to make the footage more suitable for AI processing.
The procurement has already been bid out, he said, and more cameras will also be purchased annually as the PNP expands the use of the technology among its personnel.
For his part, Nartatez said the cameras would also serve as protection for police officers by providing an objective record of what happens during encounters and operations.
“This technology will protect not only the public but also our police officers by providing an objective record of what transpired during police encounters and operations,” the PNP chief said.
He said the police organization would make sure that the equipment is used properly and within existing rules.

“We assure the public that these body cameras will be used to strengthen transparency and accountability in police operations. We will ensure that our personnel use the technology properly and in accordance with existing laws and policies,” Nartatez added.

articles.title: Norway’s King Harald dies aged 89
articles.summary:
Monarch’s death comes at turbulent time for royal family over association of crown princess with Jeffrey Epstein

King Harald V of Norway, Europe’s oldest reigning monarch, has died aged 89,…

blocks.text: King Harald V of Norway, Europe’s oldest reigning monarch, has died aged 89, the royal palace in Oslo has announced. He was succeeded immediately by his son, King Haakon VIII.

“It is with deep sadness that we announce that His Majesty King Harald passed away today. King Harald passed away peacefully at Oslo University hospital on Friday 28 August at 6.35am,” the palace said in a statement.

The new king, whose wife, Mette-Marit, has recently come under scrutiny over scandals including a much-criticised association with the late US child sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, formally notified the government of his father’s death on Friday.

As crowds gathered outside the royal palace to pay their respects, the government announced a period of national mourning. Flags around the country were lowered to half mast and church bells rang out at midday.

Haakon, 53, formally told government ministers of his father’s death at an extraordinary council of state on Friday morning. As expected, he said he would take the name Haakon VIII, and he chose the personal motto: “Everything for Norway”.

The new king will swear an oath of accession in parliament within the next few days. Coronation ceremonies were abolished in Norway more than a century ago, but Haakon could choose to have his reign blessed at a consecration ceremony.

The palace had said on Thursday that Harald’s health had deteriorated and that the king, who was seen as a unifying figure and a force for stability amid a string of recent family scandals, was in an “extremely serious” condition.

blocks.caption: King Harald during a welcoming ceremony for the Danish king and queen in Oslo in May 2024. Photograph: Per Ole Hagen/Getty Images

blocks.text: Norway’s prime minister, Jonas Gahr Støre, said he had received the news “with deep sadness”. “A whole nation is in mourning, and ⁠the people of Norway are left with a ​deep sense of ‌gratitude for a ‌long life in the service of Norway,” he said.
Støre added: “Harald V demonstrated an unwavering faith in the Norwegian people. He helped us to see the best in ourselves, and in one another … King Harald loved Norway. And Norway loved its king.”

Royalty around Europe sent their condolences, with Spain’s royal family hailing Harald’s “responsibility, dignity, humility and tireless dedication”, and Denmark’s King Frederik and Queen Mary saying he was “loved like few others”.

King Carl XVI Gustaf, of Sweden, said: “Throughout the years, King Harald has been a good friend to me, my family, and to Sweden … I ​wish ​my dear godson Haakon, ​who now succeeds his father as head ​of state, ‌success and ​good ​fortune.”

Belgium’s royal family recalled Harald’s “humour, humanity and sincerity”, while Britain’s King Charles mourned the loss of his “dear cousin”, paying tribute to a “towering figure” who guided his country with “warmth and humility”.

blocks.caption: People gather at Palace Square in Oslo to pay their respects to King Harald. Photograph: Rune Hellestad/Getty

blocks.text: The European Commission chief, Ursula von der Leyen, said he “brought Norwegians together”. Germany’s chancellor, Friedrich Merz, said Norway had “lost a great figure who stood for prudence and unity”, and the French president, Emmanuel Macron, expressed “deep sadness”.
Norway’s ceremonial head of state since 1991, Harald was being treated for haemolytic anaemia, a condition caused by an abnormally rapid destruction of the body’s red blood cells.

He had had numerous health problems – an operation for bladder cancer in 2003 and a pacemaker fitted in 2024 – but always ruled out abdicating, saying he had taken a lifelong oath before the Norwegian parliament.

His death comes amid a turbulent period for Norway’s royal family. Documents published in the US in January showed that Mette-Marit corresponded with Epstein between 2011 and 2014, long after he was convicted.

blocks.caption: Haakon had taken on additional royal duties while his father was ill. Photograph: Per Ole Hagen/Getty

blocks.text: The files appeared to contain almost 1,000 mentions of Mette-Marit, including intimate exchanges. They drew fierce public criticism, with Støre accusing her in unprecedented comments of “poor judgment”.
after newsletter promotion

Mette-Marit subsequently released a statement via the royal household expressing her “deepest regret for my friendship with Jeffrey Epstein” and apologising for “the situation that I have put the royal family in, especially the king and queen”.

blocks.caption: Mette-Marit had a successful lung transplant in July. Photograph: Lise Åserud/NTB Scanpix/AP

blocks.text: Marius Borg Høiby, 29, Mette-Marit’s son from a previous relationship, has also been in the spotlight after being sentenced in June to four years in prison for two rapes and 32 other charges, including violence against a former partner. He has appealed.

The scandals have affected public support for Norway’s monarchy, with a poll in February finding support down to 54% from 72% in 2024. Several polls found nearly half of the population felt Mette-Marit could not become queen.

Harald was seen as the Norwegian monarchy’s great moderniser, revamping the crown estates and changing the way the court is run. He married Sonja, a commoner, in 1968 and welcomed two others, Mette-Marit and Ari Behn, as the spouses of his children.

A great-great-grandchild ‌of Britain’s Queen Victoria, he succeeded his father, Olav V, at the age of 54 after studying at Oxford and representing his country in sailing events at the Tokyo, Mexico City and Munich Olympics. He was widely appreciated in Norway for his unassuming lifestyle and commitment to national unity.

blocks.caption: Haakon and Mette-Marit watching the 2026 World Cup match between Norway and Brazil. Photograph: The royal court/AFP/Getty

blocks.text: In an emotional speech in 2011 after the far-right extremist Anders Behring Breivik killed 77 in two terror attacks, he told his subjects that “freedom is stronger than fear” and as “a father, grandfather and spouse, I can only begin to sense some of the pain you feel. As king of the nation, I feel for every one of you.”

In a widely praised 2016 speech, he lauded diversity, tolerance and LGBTQ+ rights, saying Norwegians came from Afghanistan and Pakistan, believed “in God, in Allah and in nothing”, and included “girls who love girls, boys who love boys and girls and boys who love each other”.

blocks.caption: King Harald and Queen Sonja at the 2026 Winter Olympics in Milan, Italy. Photograph: Heiko Junge/Reuters

blocks.text: Mette-Marit, 53, who has a serious lung disease and had a transplant in July, was a single mother to Høiby, who was four years old when her engagement to Norway’s crown prince was announced in late 2000.

The marriage, which marked the first time in modern European history that a direct heir to a throne had brought a stepson into a royal family, caused huge controversy in Norway but was strongly backed by King Harald and Queen Sonja.

Mette-Marit acknowledged having what she described as a rebellious youth and prior drug use, holding an emotional press conference a week before the wedding in which she expressed regret for her choices and strongly condemned drug use.

articles.title: Suguilon assumes post as new PRO 13 chief
articles.summary: CAMP RAFAEL C. RODRIGUEZ, Butuan City – Brig. Gen. Rolindo M. Suguilon has been designated regional director of the Police Regional Office 13 (PRO 13) based here effective Friday, Aug. 28. Suguilon…

blocks.text: CAMP RAFAEL C. RODRIGUEZ, Butuan City – Brig. Gen. Rolindo M. Suguilon has been designated regional director of the Police Regional Office 13 (PRO 13) based here effective Friday, Aug. 28.
Suguilon officially assumed command of PRO 13 during a turnover of office ceremony held at the police regional headquarters PRO 13 Multi-Purpose Center here.

Police Lt. Gen. Bernard M. Banac, Deputy Chief PNP for Administration (TDCA), served as the Presiding Officer on behalf of the Chief of the Philippine National Police, Police General Jose Melencio C. Nartatez, Jr.

A member of the Philippine National Police Academy (PNPA) “Patnubay” Class of 1995, Brig. Gen. Suguilon previously served as director of the PNP Training Service (PNPTS) prior to his assignment in Northeastern Mindanao or The Caraga Region.

In his assumption message, the new top poliee official in Northestern Mindanao assured the public that he will protect, preserve, and sustain the hard-earned peace established by his predecessors at the helm of the Caraga region police force.

“To the people of Caraga, I embrace this command as a solemn commitment to God, country, and the Filipino people,” Brig. Gen. Suguilon said, adding “Together—as one disciplined, dedicated, and community-centered police force—let us build a safer, more peaceful, and more prosperous Caraga for all”.
Meanwhile, the outgoing Caraga Regional Director, Police Brig. Gen. Marcial Mariano P. Magistrado IV, will be reassigned to the Directorate for Comptrollership.

blocks.text: Iran missed two crucial shots from point-blank range to drop a 91-93 overtime defeat against New Zealand in the 2027 FIBA World Cup Asian qualifiers at the Mall of Asia Arena on Friday, Aug. 28.
Tall Black’s Sam Waardenburg blocked the first attempt of Team Melli’s Mohammad Amini before the Kiwis did enough to bother Alireza Sharifi on the missed putback to pull off the great escape.

New Zealand improved to a 5-2 record, catching Iran on the same slate in the Group E standings. The Iranian’s defeat also came ahead of its all-important clash against Gilas Pilipinas on Sunday, Aug. 30 on the same venue.
Shea Ili led the way for New Zealand with 24 points and six assists while Sam Mennenga had 15 points and 14 rebounds. Reuben Te Rangi had 13 while Waardenburg finished with 11.
Matin Aghajanpour paced Iran with 19 points while Mohammad Amini and Seyed Mahdi Jafari had 16 and 14, respectively.
Meanwhile, Australia whipped Syria, 123-64, to stay perfect through seven games.
Elijah Pepper torched Syria with 32 points, built on eight triples as the Boomers pulled away late in the first quarter and never looked back from there.
James Justice Jr. paced the Syrians with 21. They slid to a 2-5 slate in the standings.

Surigao del Norte Rep. Lalo Matugas and his son, former representative Bingo Matugas, are facing malversation and two counts of graft complaints before the Office of the Ombudsman over an unfinished P80.61-million road project, Assistant Ombudsman Mico Clavano said Friday.

Clavano said the complaints stemmed from the Mahihay-Tuburan Road project in Del Carmen, Surigao del Norte, which was certified as completed and fully paid despite being only about 65% to 70% accomplished.
“The findings here show that they still have pecuniary interest or financial interest in contracts funded by Congress. This is a conflict of interest,” Clavano said at a press conference.

Clavano said that since the complaints have already been filed, the Matugas father and son will not be facing preliminary investigation, where they will be asked to submit a counter-affidavit to dispute the charges.

articles.title: Japan’s JCR keeps Philippines’ A- rating, sees return to high growth
articles.summary: Tokyo-based Japan Credit Rating Agency Ltd. (JCR) maintained the Philippines’ credit rating at “A-” with a stable outlook as the debt watcher projects that the domestic economy will return to “high…

blocks.text: Tokyo-based Japan Credit Rating Agency Ltd. (JCR) maintained the Philippines’ credit rating at “A-” with a stable outlook as the debt watcher projects that the domestic economy will return to “high growth” rates, with initial signs of recovery surfacing in the second half of 2026.

Despite Philippine economic expansion slumping to a post-pandemic low of 2.6 percent in the first half due to high consumer prices and public construction delays, JCR still expects growth to rebound in the second half on the back of resumed spending and tamer inflation.
According to JCR, a stronger macroeconomic performance is on the horizon, with the agency projecting inflation-adjusted gross domestic product (GDP) growth to recover from July to December.
Local growth is expected to average around 3.5 percent, buoyed by the “recovery in public infrastructure investment and the effects of price stabilization policies.”

This projected turnaround follows a challenging first half of the year, during which unpredictable geopolitical headwinds and state spending bottlenecks stalled output expansion. Economic growth averaged 2.6 percent in the first half, marking a post-pandemic low.

Data showed the slowdown was driven by sluggish public investments and muted household consumption. Exacerbating this was inflation, which averaged 4.8 percent in the same period due to spikes in oil and food prices amid the ongoing war between the United States (US) and Iran.

Even with these pressures, JCR remains optimistic about the Philippines’ structural resilience and ongoing economic reforms. Beyond 2026, JCR is betting on improvements in the investment climate, propped up by the state’s efforts.

“JCR believes that, as the government works to improve the investment environment and advance industrial upgrading, the economy will return to high growth rates over the medium term,” it said in a rating action statement published Friday, Aug. 28.
This positive medium-term outlook is banking on the government’s commitment to restoring fiscal discipline.

To anchor investor confidence, the Marcos Jr. administration aims to lower the fiscal deficit-to-GDP ratio to 3.5 percent and the central government debt-to-GDP ratio to 63.1 percent by 2030 by streamlining government spending and pursuing major tax overhauls.
Achieving these milestones will require navigating a slower fiscal consolidation path in the near term due to recent delays in public works and elevated commodity prices.

As of end-2025, the national government’s (NG) debt ratio stood at 62.2 percent. While historically this was close to record highs, JCR noted that this level is relatively low compared with sovereigns rated in the “A” range.
JCR said the government debt-to-GDP ratio is expected to remain in the mid-60-percent range for some time before gradually declining toward the administration’s long-term targets.

Finance Secretary Frederick D. Go said the Japanese debt watcher’s nod to the country’s investment-grade rating and stable outlook “reflects the resilience of our economy and the government’s commitment to fiscal consolidation and long-term reforms.”
“It reinforces investor confidence and supports our efforts to attract investments, create quality jobs, and sustain inclusive growth,” Go further said.

Further, the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) also welcomed the credit rating affirmation, saying this “reflects continued confidence in the country’s sound fundamentals amid external headwinds,” particularly the heightened uncertainty, including the Middle East conflict.

“For its part, the BSP will continue to promote price stability, safeguard financial stability, and ensure safe and efficient payments and settlements,” the central bank said. “These efforts support sustainable growth and broader economic opportunities for Filipinos.”

articles.title: Legarda thanks Antique legislature for support
articles.summary: ILOILO CITY— Senator Loren Legarda has thanked the Antique Provincial Board for showing formal support while she is on extended medical leave abroad. This was after the Antique Provincial Board…

blocks.text: ILOILO CITY— Senator Loren Legarda has thanked the Antique Provincial Board for showing formal support while she is on extended medical leave abroad.

This was after the Antique Provincial Board passed Resolution 775-2026 that expressed the collective “sincere gratitude, appreciation, and support to Senator Legarda for her exemplary public service and significant contributions to the Filipino people, particularly to the people of Antique”.

“Malaki ang kahulugan nito sa akin, lalo na sa panahong ito, at makakaasa ang aking mga kasimanwa na mananatili akong matatag sa paglilingkod at nakatuon sa kapakanan ng Antique at ng ating bansa (This means a great deal to me, especially at this time, and my fellow Antiqueños can rest assured that I will remain steadfast in service and focused on the welfare of Antique and our country),” said Legarda in a statement.
It was in 2019 to 2022 when Legarda served as congresswoman of the Lone District of Antique, the home province of her maternal grandfather.
Legarda was replaced by her younger brother AA as congressional representative of Antique in 2022 when she won a Senate seat during the 2022 elections.
For nearly a decade, Legarda was able to bring in big ticket projects to Antique.
The resolution noted Legarda’s “meaningful connection with the Province of Antique and has supported various programs, initiatives, and advocacies that have contributed to the welfare, development.”

The resolution was introduced by Vice Governor Genevive Lim-Reyes and sponsored by Provincial Board Memebrs Gaseva V. Recopuerto, Joseph Eugene D. Alojipan, Emmanuel C. Palacios, Jr., Alfie Jay O. Niquia, Kenneth Dave B. Gasalao, and Julius Cezar O. Tajanlangit.

The collective sentiment of the provincial legislature also lauded Legarda for having “consistently championed advocacies on environmental protection, climate change adaptation and disaster resilience, cultural heritage, education, sustainable development, and the preservation of the country's natural and cultural resources.”
