articles.title: Peso pressures, core inflation may force BSP into rate hike in Q4
articles.summary: The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) could raise interest rates further in the fourth quarter unless underlying price pressures show a sustained slowing trend through the end of the year, according…

blocks.text: The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) could raise interest rates further in the fourth quarter unless underlying price pressures show a sustained slowing trend through the end of the year, according to ING Groep NV.

Deepali Bhargava, ING regional head of research for Asia-Pacific (APAC), said the Dutch lender expects the central bank’s Monetary Board to deliver another 25-basis-point increase in key borrowing costs during the final quarter as persistent risks keep the policy outlook hawkish.

“We continue to expect another 25 basis points (bps) rate hike in the fourth quarter of 2026 as policymakers remain focused on inflation risks until core inflation shows clear signs of moderation,” Bhargava said.
ING’s outlook comes on the heels of the BSP’s third consecutive quarter-point hike, which brought the benchmark rate to five percent from 4.75 percent.

“Uncertainty surrounding the severity and duration of El Niño, the persistence of higher oil prices, and the transmission of recent wage increases is unlikely to be fully resolved before then,” Bhargava said.

“More importantly, while these risks could keep headline inflation volatile over the coming months, we believe the BSP will be looking for convincing evidence that core inflation is decelerating before calling a peak in rates,” she added.
Core inflation stood at 4.2 percent in July, easing from a peak of 4.4 percent in June. However, this remains above the four percent target for both headline and core prints.
According to ING, core disinflation would provide greater confidence that second-round effects from food, energy, and wages are fading.
“Until that happens, the BSP is likely to maintain a hawkish bias and remain focused on ensuring that inflation expectations stay firmly anchored,” Bhargava said.
During its latest policy meeting, the BSP tweaked its 2026 average inflation forecast lower to 6.1 percent from 6.4 percent.

For 2027, however, it raised the forecast to 5.4 percent from 4.5 percent, keeping it well above the BSP’s two percent to four percent target range. Much of the upside risk to consumer prices stems from the potential implementation of a record-high wage hike, the scale of which caught the central bank off guard.
Headline inflation is expected to settle near the three percent target by 2028, specifically at 3.3 percent.

Despite disappointing economic growth, BSP Governor Eli M. Remolona Jr. argued that “the current monetary policy stance is not constraining activity,” pointing to a real policy rate of around 1.75 percent.
He asserted that a five percent benchmark rate is “not that high when you consider inflation expectations.”
ING, however, warned that narrowing interest rate differentials between the Philippines and the United States (US) could pressure the peso.

“This could place additional pressure on the peso, particularly at a time when US Treasury yields have risen sharply,” Bhargava noted, stressing that “the BSP is likely to remain cautious about pausing rate hikes prematurely.”
While ING remains hawkish, Singapore-based United Overseas Bank (UOB) believes the hiking cycle has ended.

UOB senior economist Julia Goh and economist Loke Siew Ting noted that interest rates are approaching “sufficiently restrictive territory,” adding that language shifts imply the central bank is not committing to another move. The BSP hopes another hike will not be needed.

Rather than signaling a prolonged tightening phase, the recent hike was a preemptive action to anchor expectations. Thus, UOB expects the BSP “to stay on hold” following its latest move, keeping the rate at 5 percent through 2027.

Meanwhile, Citi sees a higher likelihood of central bank action, warning that “the probability of inflation surprises materializing ahead of the Dec. 17 meeting...is more significant.” This scenario would require another quarter-point hike at the year's final policy meeting to tame inflation.
Citi does not, however, expect continued monetary tightening into next year, implying the terminal rate could peak and hold at 5.25 percent.

blocks.text: A streetsweeper who was injured in a cable accident in Valenzuela City received financial assistance as she continues to recover from her injuries.

blocks.caption: Mayor Wes Gatchalian visits streetsweeper “Aling Cora” at the hospital as she recovers from injuries sustained in a cable accident in Barangay Gen. T. de Leon. (Photo from Mayor Wes Gatchalian/Facebook)

blocks.text: Mayor Wes Gatchalian visits streetsweeper “Aling Cora” at the hospital as she recovers from injuries sustained in a cable accident in Barangay Gen. T. de Leon. (Photo from Mayor Wes Gatchalian/Facebook)
The victim, identified as “Aling Cora,” was injured after being struck by a cable along M. Delos Reyes Street in Barangay Gen. T. de Leon on Tuesday, Aug. 25.
Mayor Weslie “Wes” Gatchalian visited Cora and coordinated with the City Social Welfare and Development Office (CSWDO) to provide financial assistance for her immediate needs.
The company that owns the truck involved in the incident also agreed to provide an initial P200,000 in assistance to Cora’s family and shoulder expenses related to the accident.
The city government said Cora and her family will also receive medical, financial, and legal assistance while she recovers.
Closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage showed a truck catching a low-hanging cable while traveling along M. Delos Reyes Street. The cable reportedly struck and dragged Cora, causing her injuries.

blocks.caption: Mayor Wes Gatchalian meets with police and representatives of the companies involved following the cable accident that injured a streetsweeper in Barangay Gen. T. de Leon. (Photo from Mayor Wes Gatchalian/Facebook

Following the incident, Gatchalian immediately met with representatives of the companies involved and personnel from the Valenzuela City Police Station (VCPS) to discuss the accident and determine responsibility.
Authorities are still identifying the utility company that owns the cable.
During the meeting, it was also clarified that the cable did not belong to Meralco, although the pole where it was attached is owned by the power distributor.
Gatchalian ordered Meralco to inspect low-hanging cables in the area and identify other potential hazards to motorists and pedestrians.

articles.title: QC collects 240 tons of flood waste in August, lowest in 2 years
articles.summary: Quezon City collected 240.23 tons of flood waste this August following the recent southwest monsoon (Habagat), according to the Department of Sanitation and Cleanup Works of Quezon City (DSQC). The…

blocks.text: Quezon City collected 240.23 tons of flood waste this August following the recent southwest monsoon (Habagat), according to the Department of Sanitation and Cleanup Works of Quezon City (DSQC).
The volume was equivalent to 15,359 sacks of garbage collected in 58 clearing trips, significantly lower than the amounts recorded after weather disturbances in the previous two years.

DSQC reported that clearing teams collected 1,998.73 tons of flood waste in 528 trips in July 2025 following Typhoon “Crising,” while 27,484 tons were hauled in 3,371 trips in July 2024 after Typhoon “Carina” and the Habagat.
Fewer barangays and districts were also affected by flooding this year compared with previous years, DSQC said.

The decline in flood waste was attributed to the continued implementation of flood mitigation projects under the city’s Drainage Master Plan, sustained cleanup drives, and the cooperation of QCitizens.
The city government urged residents to help maintain cleanliness and order by properly disposing of their garbage and supporting local government initiatives.

articles.title: Nicola Coughlan and Matt Lucas among stars backing campaign against AI voice cloning
articles.summary:
About 80 people sign open letter to Andy Burnham calling for legislation to protect voice ownership

Nicola Coughlan, Hugh Bonneville and Matt Lucas are among a group of actors backing a…

blocks.text: Nicola Coughlan, Hugh Bonneville and Matt Lucas are among a group of actors backing a campaign against artificial intelligence voice cloning.

Save Our Voices Now, which is also being supported by Luke Evans, Jen Brister, Siobhán McSweeney and Pearl Mackie, aims to stop the practice in which AI technology is used to replicate a real person’s voice to say anything it is prompted to.
Bonneville, the star of Paddington and Downton Abbey, said: “My voice is unique, it’s mine, it’s part of my identity. So is yours. That’s worth speaking up about.”
“The quote was handwritten, not created by AI,” he added.

About 80 people have added their signatures to an open letter to the prime minister, Andy Burnham, and a Gov.uk petition has been launched to ask for everyone in Britain to be given ownership of their voice as part of their statutory rights.

The Derry Girls actor McSweeney said: “I’m deeply worried that legislation, contracts, working practices and ethics, and artists’ rights are not being considered or protected as quickly as AI technology is progressing.

“I believe that there is a way to work alongside AI and to use it as a tool that benefits us rather than rendering us obsolete. This is an existential problem and needs to be controlled legislatively as soon as possible. My voice is one of my tools.
“In order to adapt and move with technological advances, I don’t see why we should remove the human from the equation. Our audiences want that human connection. Not AI.”
The campaign claims that 28% of UK adults report they have been targeted by a voice-cloning scam.

The founder of Save Our Voices Now, Peter Caulfield, said: “In just three seconds, with the right AI system, your voice can be cloned, stolen and reinterpreted without your knowledge. It’s a Black Mirror episode, except this isn’t fiction. It’s happening right now.

“The bottom line is the government is allowing AI companies to steal and profit from artists’ voices without their consent. They are also allowing criminals to use AI to clone people’s identities and threaten everyone. We need to use our real voices now to stop it.”
In Denmark, law reforms are giving citizens legal ownership over their own face, body and voice, allowing them to demand removal of unauthorised AI content and seek compensation.

articles.title: Sarmiento urges youth to turn peace studies into practical solutions
articles.summary: Presidential Peace Adviser Mel Senen S. Sarmiento on Thursday urged students and young people to use their education to develop workable responses to the region’s peace and security concerns.…

blocks.text: Presidential Peace Adviser Mel Senen S. Sarmiento on Thursday urged students and young people to use their education to develop workable responses to the region’s peace and security concerns.

Speaking at the launch of the ASEAN Institute for Peace and Reconciliation (ASEAN-IPR) University Tour at Ateneo de Manila University on Thursday, Aug. 27, Sarmiento said universities have a key role in developing future leaders and strengthening peacebuilding efforts across Southeast Asia.

“You are not merely observers of the challenges facing our region. You will eventually become policymakers, public servants, researchers, community leaders, and perhaps peacebuilders yourselves,” Sarmiento told students of the university.

“Use your education to ask difficult questions, but also to find practical solutions. Study what works. Learn from the successes and failures of others. And when you find a good idea that can improve people’s lives, do not be afraid to adapt it, improve it, and put it to work,” he added.
The university tour was organized by the ASEAN-IPR in partnership with the Ateneo School of Government and the Office of the Presidential Adviser on Peace, Reconciliation, and Unity (OPAPRU).
It brought together students, academics, and other peace stakeholders for discussions on peacebuilding, conflict resolution, and the changing security environment in the region.
Sarmiento said the initiative was meant to bring the work of the ASEAN-IPR closer to academic institutions while creating opportunities for research, dialogue, and the sharing of experiences.

He said President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., as chair of the 2026 ASEAN Summit, had called on the ASEAN-IPR to further advance its mandate through research, advocacy, peace education and stronger engagement with universities and other stakeholders.
Marcos has also emphasized the participation of women and young people as partners in building peace, rather than simply as beneficiaries of peace efforts, Sarmiento said.
The discussions covered both traditional and non-traditional threats, including violent extremism, disinformation, cybersecurity, maritime concerns and climate-related risks.

“These challenges remind us that peace cannot be built in isolation. They require cooperation among governments, communities, universities, think tanks, and especially our young people,” Sarmiento said.

articles.title: Factory-gate prices buck easing inflation trend in July
articles.summary: Factory-gate price growth inched up in July, bucking the continued easing in headline inflation, as higher petroleum and electronics prices offset slower increases in food manufacturing prices. The…

blocks.text: Factory-gate price growth inched up in July, bucking the continued easing in headline inflation, as higher petroleum and electronics prices offset slower increases in food manufacturing prices.

The latest preliminary Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) data released on Friday, Aug. 28, showed that the producer price index (PPI) for manufacturing rose by 2.983 percent year-on-year in July, slightly faster than the revised 2.98-percent growth in June.
Producer prices had declined by 0.1 percent in July last year, while the average year-on-year PPI growth rate in the first seven months of 2026 stood at 2.4 percent.

The slight pickup in factory-gate price growth contrasted with the continued downtrend in headline inflation, which eased to 6.2 percent in July from 6.4 percent in June, 6.8 percent in May and the more-than-three-year high of 7.2 percent in April as the war in the Middle East dragged on.
Despite easing for three consecutive months, inflation remained well above the government’s two- to four-percent target range.
While consumer inflation measures changes in the prices households pay for goods and services, PPI tracks changes in the prices manufacturers receive for goods at the factory gate.

Factory-gate prices can provide an indication of underlying cost pressures in the production chain, as sustained increases in manufacturers’ prices can eventually feed into consumer prices when higher costs are passed on to buyers.
On a month-on-month basis, the seasonally adjusted PPI for manufacturing rose by 0.1 percent in July, reversing a 0.1-percent decline in June.

The PSA attributed the slight acceleration in annual factory-gate price growth mainly to coke and refined petroleum products, whose PPI growth accelerated to 2.4 percent in July from 1.3 percent in June.
The industry division accounted for 68.6 percent of the increase in the annual growth rate of manufacturing PPI during the month.

Price growth for computer, electronic and optical products also accelerated to 5.8 percent from 5.6 percent, while other manufacturing and repair and installation of machinery and equipment posted faster growth of 3.2 percent from 2.4 percent.
Overall, the manufacture of computer, electronic and optical products was the biggest contributor to the annual growth in factory-gate prices, followed by basic metals and transport equipment.
Of the 22 manufacturing industry divisions monitored by the PSA, 20 posted annual price increases in July, while two recorded declines.

Food manufacturing, however, moved in the opposite direction, with its PPI growth slowing to 1.3 percent in July from 1.7 percent in June. The rate nevertheless remained higher than the 0.7-percent increase recorded a year ago.
On a seasonally adjusted month-on-month basis, food manufacturing prices declined by 0.2 percent in July, reversing a 0.3-percent increase in June.

The PSA attributed the slowdown in annual food manufacturing PPI growth to slower price increases in five of the eight industry groups, led by prepared animal feeds, whose growth dropped to 0.9 percent in July from 2.3 percent in June.

The slowdown was partly offset by faster increases in processing and preserving of meat, which accelerated to 1.3 percent from 1.1 percent; processing and preserving of fish, crustaceans and mollusks, to 4.6 percent from 4.1 percent; and manufacture of dairy products, to 5.4 percent from 5.2 percent.

Manufacturing producer-price growth had accelerated from 0.9 percent in January to 1.2 percent in February, 2.6 percent in March and 2.8 percent in April, before reaching 3.2 percent in May. - with a report from Danielle T. Bayani

articles.title: Project NOAH to help ensure only legit flood projects get funding, says Suansing
articles.summary: The chairperson of the House Committee on Appropriations has met with University of the Philippines (UP) officials in a bid to strengthen support for education and disaster preparedness, with Project…

blocks.text: The chairperson of the House Committee on Appropriations has met with University of the Philippines (UP) officials in a bid to strengthen support for education and disaster preparedness, with Project NOAH being the centerpiece.

Nueva Ecija 1st district Rep. Mikaela Angela "Mika" Suansing did so even as the appropriations panel was knee-deep in its per agency hearings on the P7.2-trillion General Appropriations Bill (GAB) or proposed national budget for 2027.
In particular, Suansing spoke with UP president, lawyer Angelo Jimenez on continued support for free and quality education.

She also discussed Project NOAH with UP Resilience Institute (UPRI) Executive Director Dr. Mahar Lagmay, following the allocation of P1 billion for the project under the current 2026 General Appropriations Act (GAA), which Suansing actively pushed for last year and secured with the support of the Congress.

The Committee on Appropriations chairperson expects the funding to translate to stronger flood and hazard mapping, barangay-level early warning systems, and better identification of areas that need flood mitigation.
“Katulong ang Project NOAH, sisiguraduhin po ng inyong lingkod at ng Kongreso na tanging ang mga flood control projects lamang sa flood-prone areas ang mapopondohan,” she said.
(With the help of Project NOAH, yours truly and Congress will ensure that only flood control projects in flood-prone areas will be funded.)
Project NOAH stands for Nationwide Operational Assessment of Hazards. It was launched in 2012 to improve disaster preparedness using science, mapping, and real-time data.

It's designed to monitor hazards such as floods, typhoons, landslides, and storm surges. It maps vulnerable areas and provides weather and hazard information to help with early warnings and disaster response.
Suansing also emphasized the need to carefully review projects before they are included in the final national budget.

She said the House will conduct another round of vetting during budget deliberations to ensure that flood control projects included in the final version of the budget are necessary and can be properly implemented.
The GAB, once enacted, becomes the GAA.

articles.title: Dr. Martens steps into a new chapter with Glorietta store
articles.summary: In 1945, recovering soldier Dr. Klaus Maertens created a unique air-cushioned sole to help ease the pain of his broken foot. Using a salvaged cobbler’s last and a needle, he developed the prototype…

blocks.text: In 1945, recovering soldier Dr. Klaus Maertens created a unique air-cushioned sole to help ease the pain of his broken foot. Using a salvaged cobbler’s last and a needle, he developed the prototype that would eventually become one of the world’s most recognizable footwear brands, Dr. Martens.

What began as recovery footwear eventually became a staple among working-class communities in England before finding its place in fashion and music culture. More than six decades later, the brand continues to cross borders and generations, gaining a growing following in the Philippines.

For fans in Makati City, getting a pair of “Docs,” the brand’s popular nickname, is now more convenient. Dr. Martens recently opened its newest store at Glorietta Mall, Makati City, bringing its iconic silhouettes, new designs, and expanded selection to both longtime collectors and a younger generation of customers.

The store carries some of the brand’s best-known designs, including the 1460 boots, 1461 shoes, 2976 Chelsea boots, and Adrian loafers. It also features newer franchises such as the Zebzag, Buzz, and Lowell, alongside bags, small leather goods, accessories, and shoe care products.

In an interview with Manila Bulletin Lifestyle during the store opening on Aug. 22, MAP Active Philippines senior marketing manager Cheska Perfecto said the new location offers more colors, designs, and pieces, including selections from the brand’s fall collection.
“This caters to both collectors and a new, young market, the Gen Zs and Millennials,” she said. “These young people are into loafers and are starting their Dr. Martens journey.”

For those looking beyond the classic black-and-cherry red colorways, the store also offers more playful shades. Among the pieces are the 1461 in Wild Green Razor, 2976 boots in Oxblood, and Lowell Nubuck Moc Toe shoes in Dusty Rose.

Loafers, in particular, take the spotlight this fall. The Adrian Arcadia Leather Tassel Loafers, priced at ₱13,995, offer a formal take on the classic tassel loafer in Cherry Red Arcadia leather. The style is built on Dr. Martens’ air-cushioned sole and features Goodyear-welted, heat-sealed construction.

Another option is the Penton Ben Loafer in Brown Mayhem Leather, also priced at ₱13,995. Featuring a moc toe, penny slot, deep cleats, yellow welt stitching, and a Ben sole, the loafer offers a more relaxed interpretation of the classic silhouette.

Beyond the shoes, the new store is designed to introduce customers to the details behind Dr. Martens’ footwear. Posters throughout the space explain the brand’s stitches, leathers, and signature heel loop, while a dedicated section highlights its different sole constructions, including DMS, Ben, Zebzag, Bex, and Quad.

“Zebzag is something we just released last year. True to its name, the sole is zigzag; it’s lighter, and soon the wind-bouncing sole,” Cheska explained. “It’s contrary to the idea that Dr. Martens is always hard and heavy.”

The store also gives customers a closer look at the different leathers used across the brand’s footwear, including Bex Smooth, Nappa, Virginia, and Pascal, each offering different characteristics and wearing experiences.
For fans of nostalgic pop culture, there is another reason to visit. Cheska shared that the Dr. Martens x Powerpuff Girls collection will also be available in the Philippines.

Beyond footwear, shoppers can find backpacks, handbags, and duffle bags, as well as other leather goods. More items, including card holders and shoe care products, are also set to join the store’s offerings.

From its beginnings as a solution for an injured foot to its evolution into a symbol of self-expression, Dr. Martens continues to build on its heritage while finding new ways to reach the next generation of wearers.

blocks.text: ABS-CBN picked up three honors at the 2026 ContentAsia Awards in Bangkok, with Angelica Panganiban, “Call Me Mother” and ABS-CBN Studios’ adaptation of “It’s Okay to Not Be Okay” among the winners.

Panganiban won Bronze for Best Female Lead in a TV Programme/Series Made in Asia for her performance as Jackie Carpio in the mystery-thriller series “The Silent Noise,” produced by ABS-CBN Studios and Prime Video.
Panganiban’s award adds another international recognition for the series, which previously won Best Asian Content at the 2026 Global OTT Awards in South Korea.
Meanwhile, “Call Me Mother,” starring Vice Ganda and Nadine Lustre, won Silver for Best Feature Film or Telemovie Made in Asia.
Directed by Jun Robles Lana, the comedy-drama follows a queer foster mother who wants to legally adopt her son, only to face the return of his biological mother.
ABS-CBN Studios also took home Silver for Best TV Format Adaptation (Scripted) in Asia for its Philippine adaptation of the Korean drama “It’s Okay to Not Be Okay.”
The local version stars Anne Curtis, Joshua Garcia and Carlo Aquino.
More than 500 entries were submitted for the 2026 awards, with more than 180 programs nominated across 35 categories.
The winners were selected by more than 100 jurors from the entertainment industry in Asia and other parts of the world.
Now in its seventh year, the ContentAsia Awards were held Thursday, Aug. 27, in Bangkok, Thailand.

articles.title: LIVE UPDATES: Nepal-Tibet flash flood devastation (Aug 28, 2026)
articles.summary: A huge wall of mud and rock collapsed into a river on the Himalayan border of Nepal and China's Tibet. Here's the latest updates on Friday, August 28, 2026

blocks.text: Missing Filipino in Nepal flood identified; sister asks for help
The Filipino who has been missing following the massive flood in Nepal has been identified by Nepalese authorities, as his sister now calls for help in tracing his whereabouts.
According to an official log by Nepal's Department of Tourism, Juan Carlos Manalo of the Philippines has been listed as a missing person in the wake of Wednesday's flooding.
Manalo was identified as part of a "trekkers society."
As this developed, Chaira Manalo, who identified herself as the sister of Juan Carlos, asked for information related to his current whereabouts.
PH embassy in New Delhi confirms 1 Filipino missing in Nepal flash flood
The Philippine Embassy in New Delhi, which has jurisdiction over Nepal, confirmed Friday that one Filipino was indeed missing in the wake of the massive flash flood at the Nepal-China border.
The Embassy said the family of the missing Filipino has yet to reach out to them, but they ready to assist them.
The Nepal Tourism Board Thursday posted a list of missing persons due to the flash flood. Of the 667 missing persons from 32 countries, one is from the Philippines.
PH envoy: Filipino community in Nepal safe; 1 Pinoy still missing after flood

Members of the Filipino community in Nepal are safe and have all been accounted for, while the search continues for a missing Filipino in the wake of the massive flash flood at the Nepal-China border that left hundreds dead, a Philippine envoy said Friday.

Consul General Maria Cynthia Pelayo of the Philippine Embassy in India, which represents the Philippines in Nepal, told Super Radyo dzBB that coordination is ongoing with the Filipino community in the destated country following Wednesday's flooding.

"Mayroon kaming close communication with the Filipino community in Nepal (We have close communication with the Filipino community in Nepal). Fortunately, they are all okay. They are well accounted for," Pelayo said.

The Philippines designates a non-resident ambassador to Nepal, who is based in New Delhi, India. On the other hand, the Nepalese non-resident ambassador to the Philippines is based in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia.
Filipina in Kathmandu worries about flooding, says Nepal's small PH community keeps in touch

A Filipina living in Kathmandu remains anxious after catastrophic flash floods devastated communities in Nepal's north near the Himalayan border with Tibet, an area she said is not too far from her home.

“I cannot say na sobrang layo niya kasi based on the map po, it's just 100 kilometers away," Divina, who lives in the Nepalese capital with her Nepali husband and their daughter, told GMA News. "Two to three hours' drive po siya from my place.”

A massive wall of water and mud crashed through valleys and hillsides on the border regions of Nepal and Tibet on Wednesday, and swept down a route that links Kathmandu with Lhasa in Tibet and which is usually thronged by trekkers and pilgrims. Nearly 1,000 people are still missing and at least 362 people have been killed. At least one Filipino is missing, according to Nepalese authorities.
Nepal flash flood 'unlikely' in PH —weather specialist
A weather specialist from PAGASA believes that the flash flood that occurred along the Nepal-Tibet border is unlikely to occur in the Philippines.

“Based on ‘yung ating construction ng mga kailugan po sa ngayon is somehow hindi naman ganoon ka-drastic talaga, hindi comparable doon sa nangyari sa may area ng Himalayas kasi sobrang lawak naman po atsaka ang tataas talaga ng mga bundok nila doon,” PAGASA weather specialist Benison Estareja said in an interview on Super Radyo dzBB on Friday.

(Based on the current construction of our rivers, it is somehow not that drastic and is not comparable to what happened in the Himalayan region, which is much more extensive and has much higher mountains.)

“‘Yung potential energy coming from ‘yung pinakamataas papunta sa ibaba, talagang sobra ‘yung impact. Unlike dito na, yes may tendency na talagang dumami ‘yung tubig, pero ‘yung ragasa po hindi naman siya nakikita halos maladelubyo,” he added.
1 Filipino still missing after deadly Nepal flash flood

One Filipino remains missing following the deadly flash flood that struck Nepal on Wednesday, with Philippine officials continuing to coordinate with Nepalese authorities and the Filipino community to locate the missing national.
Philippine Embassy in India Consul General Maria Cynthia Pelayo said Friday that they have yet to receive information on the Filipino whose disappearance was reported following the disaster.
“Until now, we are still waiting for information about the missing Filipino which was reported yesterday,” Pelayo said in a Super Radyo dzBB interview.
The Filipino is among the 667 foreign nationals from 32 countries listed as still missing in the update released by Nepal’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Thursday evening.
Pelayo said the Philippine Embassy has maintained close communication with the Filipino community in Nepal and that those they have accounted for are safe.
“Fortunately, they are all okay. They are well accounted for,” she said.

Most members of the Filipino community are in Kathmandu, according to Pelayo. She said around 90% of the profiles they have are spouses of Nepalese nationals, while the percentage of Filipino professionals in the country is “very minimal.”

The Philippine government earlier said there were 18 overseas Filipino workers (OFWs) in Nepal based on Overseas Workers Welfare Administration records, while Department of Foreign Affairs data showed 128 Filipinos in the country.
Rescue efforts continue
Pelayo said Nepalese authorities continue rescue operations in areas affected by the flash flood, although access to some locations remains difficult.
The Philippine official also noted that getting information from the affected areas has been difficult, saying it would be challenging for her to personally reach the location.

Nepal’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs has established an emergency response team to coordinate search and rescue operations, verify information concerning missing foreign nationals and provide consular assistance. It has also urged families and diplomatic missions to rely on official channels and avoid circulating unverified information.
The disaster was triggered by a glacier collapse that sent a torrent of water, rock, ice and mud through Himalayan river systems along the Nepal-China border.
A Reuters report on Thursday quoting the Nepali police said that 359 had died, with dozens of bodies swept down into the plains from where they were being recovered.

Rescuers searched for survivors in the debris-strewn valleys and hillsides of Nepal on Thursday while more than 1,000 people remained missing there and in neighboring China after a wall of ice, mud and rock collapsed into a mountain river, triggering a catastrophic flash flood.

articles.title: Gatchalian: Absent senators forgo salaries
articles.summary: Senators who have been absent from Senate plenary sessions either due to detention, medical problems, or other reasons have voluntarily decided not to receive their salaries. Senate President Sherwin…

blocks.text: Senators who have been absent from Senate plenary sessions either due to detention, medical problems, or other reasons have voluntarily decided not to receive their salaries.

Senate President Sherwin “Win” Gatchalian disclosed this on Thursday, August 27 saying that even Sen. Loren Legarda, who earlier filed for an extended medical leave, had also declined accepting her pay.
“When she filed for medical leave and she is also not collecting her salary. In fact, the detained senators and the senator-at-large are also voluntarily foregoing their salaries,” Gatchalian said.
Legarda earlier filed five medical leaves covering Aug. 3 to Aug. 5, Aug. 11 to Aug. 12, Aug. 17 to Aug. 19, and Aug. 24 and Aug. 26, as well as Sept. 1 to Sept. 2.
According to Gatchalian, he is aware of Legarda’s medical condition but declined to provide details about the issue.
“It's a very personal matter. I am aware of her illness; even before this, we were personal friends, and she had already confided in me about having a serious condition,” the Senate chief said.
Gatchalian said he has instructed the Senate’s accounting and payroll department to suspend the release of their salaries.
He said the Senate can declare the unused salaries as savings and use it for something else.
“I wish her well; illnesses like this really need to be taken seriously,” he said.
Legarda has not publicly disclosed the nature of her illness, but earlier, Sen. Panfilo “Ping” Lacson said that her medical leave could be related to lung problems.

Legarda and her son, Rep. Leandro Leviste, are currently facing high-profile plunder and graft complaints filed by the Office of the Ombudsman, which earlier flagged their absences as “highly suspicious.”

Both were accused of alleged irregularities and “ghost electricity” projects in connection to Leviste’s solar companies, which supposedly failed to deliver committed power generation despite securing exclusive government service contracts, resulting in billions in unpaid government obligations.

Also absent from Senate while facing plunder cases are Senators Jinggoy Estrada and Rodante Marcoleta. Sen. Ronald “Bato” Dela Rosa, on the other hand, remains at large in connection with a crimes against humanity case before the International Criminal Court (ICC).

articles.title: Paulo Avelino 'cancels' everything for GTA 6
articles.summary: A man and his priorities! Paulo Avelino had fans doing a double take after posting what looked like a serious announcement about stepping away from work. “To my fans, my kababayan, and everyone I've…

blocks.text: Paulo Avelino
A man and his priorities!
Paulo Avelino had fans doing a double take after posting what looked like a serious announcement about stepping away from work.
“To my fans, my kababayan, and everyone I've worked with:

“After a lot of prayer and some hard conversations at home, I'm stepping away from everything effective October 31. The movies, the teleserye, all my endorsements. Everything,” Paulo wrote on Instagram.
Then came the real reason.
“GTA 6 is out November 19. PoE 2 hits 1.0 on December 11, and they finally added swords. I watched the Extended Look last night, and I have not been okay since,” he continued.
Note the extended 26-minute preview of “GTA 6” was recently released, giving fans a longer look at Rockstar Games’ much-awaited title.
Paulo, apparently, was among those who were not prepared for it.
And because he is Paulo Avelino, he even had instructions for his legal team.
“To my legal counsel, please tell everyone lining up to sue me that I'm available March 2027. I'll have 100% GTA completion and a build nobody can touch by then. Sue me at my peak,” he wrote.
So there you have it.
Paulo is not really giving up the movies, teleseryes and endorsements.
At least not permanently.
He just needs some time to save Los Santos first.
Game on.

During the surrender, the rebel returnee turned over a caliber .38 revolver without serial number, and five live ammunition.

In a statement, the 3rd Maneuver Company vowed to continue its efforts and remain committed to sustain peace and order in the community.

articles.title: UEFA prepares Swiss complaint against FIFA chief Infantino over World Cup sell-off
articles.summary: MONACO (AP) — UEFA is preparing a criminal complaint against FIFA President Gianni Infantino in Swiss courts for possible financial mismanagement over his failed plan to sell future World Cup profits…

blocks.text: MONACO (AP) — UEFA is preparing a criminal complaint against FIFA President Gianni Infantino in Swiss courts for possible financial mismanagement over his failed plan to sell future World Cup profits to private investors.

The governing body of European soccer announced its intentions in court documents filed Thursday, Aug. 27, in the U.S. seeking access to possible evidence related to the sell-off plan, which was withdrawn after a furious backlash by UEFA and other global soccer leaders.
The move increases the pressure on Infantino, who is facing the biggest crisis in his 10 years as FIFA's leader.

UEFA filed documents in a Manhattan court requesting discovery of potential evidence from the New York investment fund, Thrive Capital Management, founded by Josh Kushner — the younger brother of President Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner.
UEFA also filed a request in a southern Florida district for authorization of discovery “in a foreign proceeding” against FIFA itself, which has offices in the Miami suburb of Coral Gables.

Under the plan revealed in late July, Thrive and Kushner were to be the anchor investors intending to pay FIFA $4.2 billion for a 20% stake in a subsidiary that would run the soccer body’s commercial events, including the World Cup.

“UEFA and its counsel are contemplating a Swiss criminal proceeding against Infantino and possibly other FIFA officials for criminal mismanagement under Article 158 of the Swiss Criminal Code,” UEFA’s lawyers state in a 56-page document seen by The Associated Press.
The document suggests the $4.2 billion figure could be a “fraudulently off-market price promoted by Infantino for his own benefit.”
FIFA is expected to have about $5 billion in cash reserves after the World Cup in North America boosted its revenue to a record $15 billion over the 2023-26 commercial cycle.
“The question is therefore why the FIFA president believed he needed outside investors to expand development funding,” UEFA said in a statement.
Infantino dropped the sell-off plan on Aug. 1 after intense criticism led by soccer officials in Europe.
UEFA had warned against destroying potential evidence

UEFA first threatened to take legal action on Aug. 3 when it warned FIFA against destroying or hiding any "relevant materials” related to the plan. Thursday's legal move was revealed to its member federations in Monaco just two hours before the Champions League draw began.

“Infantino claimed that the plan would ‘unleash the commercial potential and opportunity that FIFA has,’” UEFA lawyers told the courts. “In truth, it was a vehicle for Infantino and that small circle to acquire a permanent stake in and otherwise profit from FIFA’s most valuable assets to the detriment of FIFA, its members, and other parties within the football family.

“Under the terms Infantino announced, those investors stood to acquire a permanent financial interest in FIFA’s commercial arm for $4.2 billion, implying an absurdly low enterprise value of only approximately $20 billion, a figure that was neither the product of an open, competitive auction, nor tested by any independent valuer.”
Thrive declined to comment. FIFA was approached for comment.
Swiss prosecutors' poor results in FIFA trials
It was unclear if UEFA would send a potential criminal complaint to the Swiss federal prosecution office in Bern or to local prosecutors in FIFA's home city Zurich.
The Swiss attorney general's office has a poor record in recent years prosecuting cases of alleged corruption linked to FIFA and soccer officials.

Former FIFA president Sepp Blatter, former UEFA president Michel Platini and the influential Qatari president of Champions League title holder Paris Saint-Germain, Nasser al-Khelaïfi, all were acquitted twice at trials in Switzerland.
UEFA committed to replacing Infantino

The crisis has raised questions about Infantino’s future. Just months ago, he was widely expected to win another four-year term in the FIFA election set for March 2027, but a growing number of soccer federations around the world but mainly in Europe have withdrawn their support, with some joining UEFA in calling on him to step down, ideally before the Nov. 18 deadline for candidates.

“Should the current FIFA president nevertheless seek another mandate, UEFA will join forces with its partner confederations to ensure that member associations are offered a credible alternative,” the European body said, “one committed to integrity, accountability, development and genuine institutional change.”

articles.title: Filipino doctor among missing after Nepal flash floods
articles.summary: A Filipino doctor who went on a pilgrimage in Nepal has gone missing following the massive flash flood that tore through the Nepal-China border this week.

blocks.text: Juan Carlos Manalo, a Filipino traveler who joined a pilgrimate tour in Nepal, has been unreachable since the massive flash floods that hit the Nepal-China border this week.
Chiara Manalo
MANILA, Philippines – A Filipino doctor who went on a pilgrimage in Nepal has gone missing following the massive flash flood that tore through the Nepal-Tibet border this week.

Physician Juan Carlos Manalo was traveling with a group of pilgrims when the series of flash floods and subsequent landslides took place. He has been unreachable since, according to a Facebook post by his sister, Chiara Manalo.
Chiara said the family last heard from Juan Carlos on Tuesday, August 25, at 1:21 p.m. Philippine time, a day before the floods struck.
The group's last known location was the immigration office in Gyirong, on the Tibetan side of the border, Chiara said.
Juan Carlos had been traveling with a Kailash Mansarovar Yatra pilgrimage group organized by the Isha Foundation, an India-based spiritual organization, led by Sadhguru Jaggi Vasudev

Sadhguru said in a social media post Wednesday that 77 pilgrims from one of his Kailash groups were at the Gyirong immigration office, on their way back from the pilgrimage, when the flood struck and swamped the building and much of the town. He said there was no official information yet on their whereabouts.
Chiara told Philstar.com her brother had spent the past couple of years volunteering as a medical worker at an Isha Foundation center in India, and had gone there in May, by her recollection.
He joined this year's Kailash tour around August 6 or 8, Manalo said.
Juan Carlos had usually sent updates to his family every day until their parents got a call on the night of August 26 about the floods.
Chiara said she reached out to the group's Philippine contact person and was told her brother's group was at the immigration office — on its way back to India — when the flash flood hit.
The family is asking anyone with information to contact their family: Jose Rodrigo Manalo (+63 917 302 3077), Dinah Marie Manalo (+63 917 514 3465), or Chiara Manalo (+63 917 791 7849).
Manalo appears to be the Filipino traveler the Nepal Tourism Board has counted among hundreds of missing foreigners since Thursday.

The Department of Foreign Affairs said on Friday the Philippine Embassy in New Delhi and the honorary consulate in Kathmandu were coordinating with Nepali authorities and are "awaiting confirmation from Nepali authorities on a Filipino national who is reported missing."
The massive August 26 floods were set off by a glacier collapse in the Himalayas that triggered a landslide and sent an avalanche of water, ice and debris.

More than 300 people have been confirmed dead and hundreds more remain missing in Nepal, with additional deaths and missing reported on the Chinese side of the border, according to the latest tallies.

articles.title: DILG flags grooming, extremist content targeting minors on Roblox
articles.summary: The Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) on Friday raised alarm over alleged online grooming and extremist conversations targeting minors on Roblox.

blocks.text: Published August 28, 2026 2:08pm
Make this your preferred source to get more updates from this publisher on Google.
The Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) on Friday raised alarm over alleged online grooming and extremist conversations targeting minors on Roblox.

“The Roblox games are played by millions of teenagers here in the Philippines. So that should be stopped. Sa Roblox namin nakita ang extremist conversations,” DILG Secretary Jonvic Remulla said during a press conference.

“Yun sa ibang first person shooters game, hindi pa namin nakikita as extensive as what you see in Roblox. At saka international ‘yan. International ang scale ng groomers na nangyayari dito,” he added.

Authorities have observed chat groups on the gaming platform and found some of the language used in these online conversations was allegedly criminal in nature and involved incitement of teenagers to violence.
Other Stories
Remulla earlier expressed his support to impose a total ban against Roblox following the fatal shooting at Ateneo de Zamboanga University on August 18.
In March, Roblox expressed its commitment to maintaining the safety of children, including its Filipino users, on the platform.
The company emphasized that "advanced safeguards and robust safety policies" are already in place to protect its players.

“We have filters designed to block the sharing of personal information, our chat features don’t allow user-to-user image or video sharing, and age checks are required before anyone has access to chat," Roblox said.

"Those same checks are also used to limit kids and teens to only chatting with others of similar age by default. Our approach includes multiple layers of protection: advanced AI detection systems, dedicated teams who constantly monitor for critical harms, user reporting tools, and ongoing collaboration with law enforcement and safety organizations,” the company added. —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: DILG probes BFP officials over alleged ‘slots for sale’ scheme
articles.summary: DILG chief Jonvic Remulla warned all BFP officials involved in the 'slots for sale' scheme to come out and confess as crack down begins.

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — All former and current regional directors of the Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP) are under investigation as the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) cracks down on the alleged widespread "slots for sale" extortion scheme within the fire agency.

Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla said in a press briefing at Camp Crame, Quezon City, on Friday, August 28, that more than 200 fire personnel nationwide are under investigation for alleged involvement in what he described as a long-standing “cancer” in the BFP.
“The BFP has become a criminal syndicate instead of a law enforcement and a first responder,” Remulla said.
Remulla’s warning

The "slots for sale" scheme was previously uncovered by the DILG in February this year, in which some officials allegedly required BFP applicants to pay hundreds of thousands of pesos in exchange for guaranteed promotion or acceptance.
Remulla said those involved typically require payments ranging from P100,000 to P800,000.
“Binabalaan ko na ang lahat ng opisyal ng BFP. Lumabas na kayo ngayon at umamin kayo o hahabulin namin kayo hanggang matapos ang career n’yo,” Remulla warned.
(I am warning all the BFP officials. Come out and confess or we will come after you until the end of your careers.)
Remulla stressed that not all regional directors are restricted from their duties during the investigation, but only those who are proven to have links to corruption.
Crackdown

Remulla’s warning came following the arrest of a female BFP personnel earlier this week during an entrapment operation in San Fernando City, Pampanga, after an applicant made a report to the authorities.

The suspect, who was identified as a 32-year-old active Senior Fire Officer 1, allegedly used a dummy account to contact an aspiring Fire Officer 1 and demanded P500,000 in exchange for a guaranteed slot.

She was arrested by the Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (CIDG) on August 24 while receiving the partial payment of P300,000 from the complainant. She is currently under the custody of the CIDG.

The CIDG said a criminal complaint for robbery-extortion in relation to Republic Act 10175, or the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012, was filed against the suspect before the San Fernando City prosecutors on August 26.
The involved senior officer, who was identified as Deputy Regional Director for Administration in Region 4A, has also been relieved of his post.
“Hindi lang po matatapos ito dito. We are going after the entire institution, all the rotten eggs,” Remulla said.
(This will not end here, we are going after the entire institution, all the rotten eggs)
BFP Officer-in-Charge Wilberto Kwan Tiu stressed in the same press briefing that the BFP will not require any payment from its applicants.
“Inuulit ko po, walang bayad ang pagpasok sa aming ahensya. Libre po ito,” Kwan Tiu said.
(I repeat, there’s no payment required to join our agency. This is free)
‘Syndicates’
Kwan Tiu said they have since implemented electronic hiring systems to address the slots for sale scheme.
He, however, admitted that as the agency’s systems evolve, the modus of those involved in the scheme also adapts.
Remulla, meanwhile, said the CIDG has already subpoenaed the fire officers who were identified as beneficiaries of the slots for sale scheme as part of the further investigation.
“They can either testify kung ano ang nangyari, or we can charge them because we already saw conclusive links na nagbayad sila,” Remulla said.
Remulla added that those who testify may be given clemency and can continue their service, as long as they will “spill all the beans”. Otherwise, they will be dismissed.
When asked if he can eradicate the corruption issue in the BFP under his term, Remulla said the DILG will remove the "syndicates" within six months.
“Sa PNP tinanggal na natin lahat ng sindikato. Within the BFP matatanggal ko rin lahat ng sindikatong ito,” Remulla said.
(We have already removed all the syndicates from the PNP. I will also remove all these syndicates from the BFP.)

articles.title: Selena Gomez pushes back against 'frivolous' fraud claims
articles.summary: Selena Gomez's lawyer says the fraud case is "absurd" - but it is far from unusual for celebrity family business relationships to go wrong.

blocks.text: Selena Gomez's social media accounts brim with adoring fans: two million likes for her most recent post showing her and her husband in a rose-petal strewn hotel, and thousands of comments praising her beauty, her lipstick and the perfume brand she founded.

This week the PR focus for the star – who rose to fame on the Disney channel but has moved into song-writing, films and TV drama – was supposed to be on the upcoming series six of Only Murders in the Building that sees its podcasting sleuths transfered to London for their next adventure.

But the wider chat, outside those friendly spaces, has gone off-script and is largely on a less flattering topic, namely claims from investors who allege she breached her contract by not properly backing the mental health platform Wondermind that she cofounded with her mother five years ago. As a result, the five investors argue, they were defrauded of the nearly $1.2m they invested.

Gomez is pushing back against those allegations - her lawyer has asked that she be dismissed from the case altogether, saying the claims made against her are "threadbare" and arguing she should never have been "dragged into" the case at all.

The investors claim they were told that "Selena Gomez, one of the most famous women on earth, with a billion-dollar brand and a platform unmatched in social media, would be actively building the company as its head of marketing".

Gomez's attorney Matthew Rosengart says their allegations are "vague, generalised and contradictory" and that Gomez never agreed to, and did not, manage the company, or make the kind of commitments they are suggesting.
"The claims against her are meritless if not frivolous," he said.
Mr Rosengart added that the legal team was "exploring other avenues of relief for Ms. Gomez including sanctions against plaintiffs".

The emphatic pushback from Gomez may reflect a concern for her reputation but it also leaves her mother in the hot-seat, facing the fraud allegations alongside the company itself and a third co-founder.

Crisis PR commentator, Lauren Beeching, founder of Honest London says Gomez is far from the first celebrity to try working with a close family member. At times it can come off like in the Jenner-Kardashian household or with the tennis-playing Williams sisters.
But there are plenty of examples - from the Beckhams' to Britney Spears - where family brands and business don't mix well.
Working with close relatives, whether that's a sibling or a parent, or someone else is almost always a higher risk approach, says Beeching.
"It can make the boundaries between the personal relationship with the business and the celebrity's reputation much harder to separate," she says.
The natural level of trust means that you might not apply the same rules as you would in a normal commercial relationhsip, so better guardrails are needed, she says.
"If you're going into business [as a] family, I'd put more structure around it, not less, for sure.
"Define everybody's responsibilities, bring in independent oversight, and decide what happens if something goes wrong before something goes wrong."
"A family relationship shouldn't be a company's governance structure."
At the end of the day Gomez may not need to worry too much over this case, says Beeching.
"This will generate headlines because Selena Gomez is enormously famous, but I don't think it's the type of story her core audience is particularly interested in," she says.
"There's an important difference between generating negative headlines and causing lasting reputational damage. "
Still, for celebrities considering trading on their personal brand, Beeching does have words of advice.
"Before lending your name to a company, don't ask what your reputation could do for the business. Ask what that business can eventually do for your reputation as well."

articles.title: Trump orders Lake Ontario to be renamed ‘Lake America’
articles.summary: WASHINGTON, United States — US President Donald Trump stepped up an escalating feud with Canada on Thursday, ordering that Lake Ontario — a body of water shared by both countries — be renamed…

blocks.caption: A Canadian flag flies along the waterfront of Lake Ontario, in Toronto, Ontario, Canada, on August 27, 2026. (Photo by Cole Burston / AFP)

blocks.text: WASHINGTON, United States — US President Donald Trump stepped up an escalating feud with Canada on Thursday, ordering that Lake Ontario — a body of water shared by both countries — be renamed “Lake America.”
Trump signed an executive order on the name change at the White House, further trolling Canada as the North American neighbors plunge deeper into a trade war.
“We’re going to be changing the name of Lake Ontario effective immediately to Lake America,” Trump told reporters in the Oval Office.
Behind Trump’s desk were two maps of the US-Canada border — one with the words “Lake America” in red over the lake, and the other with the header “Making the Great Lakes Even Greater.”
Asked why he was targeting an ally for punishment instead of America’s adversaries, Trump replied: “The Canadian officials have treated us very badly. They’re nasty people.”
“People, oftentimes, they’ll ask me who’s the worst to deal with on trade? And I said that’s easy. Canada. They are the worst to trade with,” the 80-year-old Republican added.

Canada did not immediately comment but is unlikely to accept the renaming of Lake Ontario, the smallest of the five Great Lakes by surface area, which borders Canada’s Ontario province and New York state.
US-Canada trade talks collapsed at the eleventh hour last week, with Trump’s tariffs taking effect on Saturday.
Canada responded with tit-for-tat tariffs on Tuesday, with Prime Minister Mark Carney saying: “You’re at war when you get attacked. We got attacked.”
The same day, Trump announced that he was giving “serious consideration” to changing the name to Lake America.
He then posted a TikTok video late Wednesday saying that he intended to do so after all.
‘Now all we need is an ocean’
The name change mirrors Trump’s unilateral altering of the name of the Gulf of Mexico to the Gulf of America on his first day back in office in January 2025.
That change obliged the US federal government to refer to the gulf by the new designation, although Mexico has rejected any move to rename it and it lacks international recognition.

Trump said the name change was “something I’ve been thinking about for a long time, actually. As you know, we took something called the Gulf of Mexico, we changed it, and now it’s very routinely the Gulf of America.”
Trump also hinted at renaming oceans that border the United States.

“So, if you think about it, we have a gulf, and we have a lake. Now all we need is an ocean. So, maybe we’ll have to change the name of the Atlantic and/or the Pacific. Maybe we’ll change them both,” he said.

While Lake Ontario shares its name with the Canadian province, the name itself is derived from the indigenous Huron word “Ontari’io,” which means “great lake” or “beautiful water,” according to the National Museum of the Great Lakes.
Toronto, Canada’s largest city, sits on its northwestern shore.
During his second presidential term, Trump has irked a series of allies with his outlandish territorial claims, including that Canada should become the 51st US state.
Trump has also laid claim to Greenland, an autonomous territory of NATO ally Denmark, and talked about making Venezuela a state following the US capture of its leader Nicolas Maduro.

articles.title: Norway holds its breath as King Harald’s health deteriorates
articles.summary: OSLO, Norway – Norway’s royal family gathered Thursday at King Harald V’s bedside in hospital, while hundreds paid respects outside the palace, after the court announced that the…

blocks.text: OSLO, Norway – Norway’s royal family gathered Thursday at King Harald V’s bedside in hospital, while hundreds paid respects outside the palace, after the court announced that the 89-year-old monarch’s health condition was “extremely serious”.

Queen Sonja and Harald’s 53-year-old son Crown Prince Haakon, who is acting as regent, have cancelled all royal engagements and spent much of Thursday at his side at Oslo University Hospital along with other family members.
The palace said late Thursday afternoon the king’s condition was “unchanged”, shortly after Haakon, his wife Mette-Marit and their two adult children were seen leaving the hospital.
Norwegian broadcaster NRK then on Thursday evening reported that Haakon and Mette-Marit had returned to the hospital a second time.

Europe’s oldest reigning monarch has been in hospital in Oslo since August 17 suffering from haemolytic anaemia, a condition caused by an abnormally rapid destruction of red blood cells which leads to fatigue and shortness of breath.
“His Majesty the King’s health condition is extremely serious,” the palace said, providing no specific details.

Mette-Marit’s son from a previous relationship, Marius Borg Hoiby, who is under house arrest and wearing an ankle bracelet after a rape conviction in June that he has appealed, was also seen leaving the hospital after a more than four-hour visit, as was the king’s sister.
Hundreds of people gathered outside the palace in central Oslo, with many laying down bouquets of flowers for the broadly popular king in front while staying for hours.
“He is Norway’s grandfather,” 57-year-old Trine Bakke Jord told AFP, adding that she appreciated that he was so “down-to-earth” while wiping away tears.
Kaspara Bolstad, 24, told AFP Harald had been “a very steady and warm king”.

“I think the entire Norwegian people see him as a role model and as someone who brings people together. Whether you’re for or against the monarchy, I think he’s well-liked across the board,” she said.
Magnus Skaugseth, 27, agreed, lauding the king’s “inclusive” side.
“When there is so much division and polarization, he was a pillar pointing in the opposite direction.”

Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store, who cancelled a work trip to Germany on Thursday following the update on the king’s health, told AFP he was “deeply affected” by the news of the king’s health condition.
“I stand together with the entire country as we now send our warmest thoughts to the king and the rest of the royal family,” he said.
Church of Norway bishops also cut short a study visit to Rome where they had met Pope Leo and were to return to Norway Thursday, according to Christian newspaper Vart Land.

Caroline Vagle, a royal reporter for the Se og Hor magazine, called Thursday’s statement from the palace “dramatic”, noting that it was usually “very restrained in its communication about the King’s health, even when he has been hospitalised or undergone treatment.”
“There is also an entire nation that is deeply concerned and saddened. King Harald is a much-loved king,” she told AFP.
The monarch was admitted to Oslo University Hospital due to fluid retention from cortisone treatment he was receiving.

articles.title: Overstaying Chinese nat’l with alleged POGO ties nabbed in Bacolod
articles.summary: BACOLOD CITY —A 34-year-old Chinese national allegedly linked to illegal Philippine offshore gaming operations (POGO) was arrested by immigration and police authorities in Bacolod City, the Bureau of…

blocks.caption: A 34-year-old Chinese national allegedly linked to illegal Philippine offshore gaming operations (POGO) was arrested by immigration and police authorities in Bacolod City, the Bureau of Immigration (BI) said Thursday, Aug. 27, 2026. INQUIRER FILE

blocks.text: BACOLOD CITY —A 34-year-old Chinese national allegedly linked to illegal Philippine offshore gaming operations (POGO) was arrested by immigration and police authorities in Bacolod City, the Bureau of Immigration (BI) said Thursday.

BI identified the suspect as Xie Yingwen, who was arrested along Yulo Street in Barangay 16 outside a residential area during an operation conducted by BI agents with the Negros Occidental Police Provincial Office and Bacolod City Police Station 1.
The operation was carried out pursuant to a mission order issued by Immigration Commissioner Joel Anthony Viado on Aug. 6.
BI said Xie was declared an overstaying and undesirable alien after he failed to present valid identification and documents showing a visa extension.
During the operation, Xie also admitted that he had previously worked in Manila as a food and fruit vendor, the agency said.
The BI said the arrest was part of the government’s continuing crackdown on illegal foreign nationals and individuals allegedly involved in unauthorized activities in the country.
Xie was subsequently transferred to the BI’s holding facility in Bicutan, Taguig City, where he remained in custody pending deportation proceedings./coa

articles.title: About 90 Americans unaccounted for in Nepal-Tibet catastrophic floods
articles.summary: McMINNVILLE, Tenn — US officials said about 90 American citizens remained unaccounted for Thursday, a day after catastrophic flash floods engulfed a border area of China and Nepal, killing hundreds…

blocks.caption: A government helicopter conducts a rescue mission amidst the devastation left by flash flooding in Nepal’s Nuwakot district, Thursday, Aug. 27, 2026. (AP Photo/Rajesh Kumar Singh)

blocks.text: McMINNVILLE, Tenn — US officials said about 90 American citizens remained unaccounted for Thursday, a day after catastrophic flash floods engulfed a border area of China and Nepal, killing hundreds of people. A spiritual organization said that 22 Americans associated with it were unaccounted for.
In a statement, the US State Department said it is not aware of any US deaths, but three Americans have been rescued.
Many of the missing were on a pilgrimage to Mount Kailash in Tibet, a sacred site for Hindus, Buddhists and others.

Social media posts were surfacing Thursday from loved ones pleading for people to provide updates or circulate information about Americans they had lost contact with — a Virginia woman traveling with a tour group, a Texas couple on a birthday trip and a mother accompanying her 14-year-old daughter.
Among those on a guided tour was Venus Rajnikant Patel, a 45-year-old Indian-born US citizen who recently moved from St. Louis to Cincinnati to help his family.

Patel’s brother, Dennis, said Venus called him and their parents a few hours before the floods, showing them his hotel room on the Nepalese side of the border and talking about how excited he was to cross into Tibet. He had been planning the pilgrimage for two years, his brother said.

Another American who is missing is 72-year-old Jitendra Patel, a Long Island resident who was with a tour group on a Hindu pilgrimage to Mount Kailash, according to his son, Sunny Patel. Jitendra last called Wednesday morning local time on WhatsApp to say that he had crossed the border into Tibet.

When Sunny first saw video of the flooding he thought no one could survive it, Sunny said. He then contacted his mother to ask about his father’s whereabouts. His mother said Jitendra was in the exact same area as the flooding.
“My heart sank,” Sunny said, adding that he “didn’t think it was possible that my dad would be there at ground zero.”
“It gets worse by every hour, obviously,” he added.

Indian spiritual guru Jaggi Vasudev, also known as Sadhguru, said in a post on X that 77 people returning from Mount Kailash with groups organized by his Isha Foundation were at an immigration center in Gyirong, Tibet, when the floods struck.

Leslie Crespi, a community liaison for the foundation’s US campus, said that 22 of them were Americans affiliated with the foundation and that three volunteers supporting the trekkers were also at the immigration center when the floods hit.
“We had communication with the coordinator of the group at about 9:05 Nepalese time saying that they had arrived there. And then by 9:14 is when this flash flood hit,” Crespi said.

The Isha Foundation is a spiritual organization based in India and its US campus, the Isha Institute of Inner-sciences, is a yoga and meditation retreat center located in the mountains near McMinnville, Tennessee.

At a candlelight vigil in New York City on Thursday, Tak Ruwali, a Long Island resident who is from one of the Nepalese districts affected by the flooding, said that he is talking with people in Nepal and many regional tourist guides are “out of contact now.”
“It means they are probably gone,” Ruwali added.
Talking to reporters in the Oval Office on Thursday, President Donald Trump said US officials have spoken with Nepalese leaders and offered to provide “anything they want.”

articles.title: Trump once saw quick end to Iran war, now says he’s in no hurry
articles.summary: WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump arrives at an awkward moment for his presidency on Friday as the U.S.-Israel war against Iran reaches the six-month mark, a notable milestone for a conflict that…

blocks.caption: President Donald Trump gestures as he walks to board Marine One on the Ellipse, Friday, Aug. 14, 2026, near the White House in Washington. — Photo by Associated Press

blocks.text: WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump arrives at an awkward moment for his presidency on Friday as the U.S.-Israel war against Iran reaches the six-month mark, a notable milestone for a conflict that the Republican leader repeatedly assured Americans would be a “little excursion” lasting a matter of weeks.
The war isn’t over, though Trump claims that through bombs and blockade, he has already devastated Iran’s leadership, military and economy.

And this week his administration said it would turn its focus to increasing economic pressure — rather than military action — to try to finish off Iran. The shifting strategy centers on threats to punish any country or entity that continues to conduct business with Tehran.

The turn to using sanctions as the cudgel of choice comes as the administration weighs diminished munitions stockpiles after months of war, sparking concerns that the prolonged conflict could undermine U.S. military readiness in other parts of the globe.

As the conflict grinds on, Trump’s talk of finding a quick end to the war also appears to be fading. He stressed this week that he’s “not in a hurry” to get Iran back to the negotiating table, and he continues making the case that the Islamic Republic’s leadership is on the ropes.

“They’re not paying their troops. They’re in deep trouble. They have very little capacity,” Trump told reporters Thursday. “We don’t want to speak to them. We’re not looking to meet or anything,” he said.

It’s unclear how — or if — Trump will address the six-month anniversary of a conflict that has already cost the United States more than $37.5 billion and done damage to his popularity ahead of critical November elections for his party. The president is spending Friday in Houston, where he’ll honor the Artemis II NASA crew for their 10-day mission around the moon earlier this year.
Trump is declaring ‘mission accomplished’ — a phrase that hurt a Republican predecessor

On its face, the moment is complicated for the “America First” leader who fiercely criticized his White House predecessors for wasting American taxpayer money and U.S. troops’ lives in Middle East conflicts and vowed on the campaign trail to keep the military out of “endless wars.”

But Trump has bristled at suggestions that this war — in which no American troops have deployed into Iran — can be compared to the yearslong wars in Iraq and Afghanistan in which more than 7,000 Americans were killed.

His Republican predecessor, President George W. Bush, was widely mocked for a 2003 speech aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln beneath a White House-produced banner that read “Mission Accomplished.” It came to symbolize a premature declaration of victory for the Iraq War, which would go on for nearly nine more years. More than two decades later, there are still U.S. troops stationed in Iraq.

Trump’s war has stretched on far longer than he told Americans it would. It didn’t stop him from sharing a social media post this week declaring “MISSION ACCOMPLISHED 2026.” The AI-generated image features Trump against a backdrop of U.S. fighter jets, a warship and American flags above smaller images of Bush and former Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, who was killed in an Israeli strike in the opening salvos of the war.

Trump has consistently emphasized that the U.S. and Israel campaign has been devastating for Iran’s navy and air force. Iranian officials have said the country has suffered $270 billion in direct and indirect damage. Israeli military strikes in the first weeks of the war wiped out much of the theocratic government’s leadership structure, including Khamenei.

But Iran has found leverage through its own strikes in the critical Strait of Hormuz, where relatively few vessels carrying oil and liquefied natural gas are risking passage. Trump again declared Thursday that the “Strait of Hormuz is open,” saying 24 vessels passed through a day earlier. That’s a fraction of the roughly 130 vessels that passed through the vital waterway daily before the war began.
Trump is showing little interest in talks

Mediators Qatar and Pakistan continue to press for a diplomatic off-ramp from the two sides. Qatar’s prime minister, Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, was in Tehran on Thursday to discuss a proposed plan between Iran and Oman to boost traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.

But in Washington, Trump has shown little interest in getting back to the preliminary deal reached in June that aimed to reopen the strait and launch talks about Iran’s nuclear program. That deal fell apart within weeks after Iran started attacking ships.

At the same time, Trump says the U.S. effort to economically choke off Tehran is working, with a U.S. naval blockade preventing Iranian oil from making it to market as the trickle of vessels carrying oil from other Gulf nations pass through.
“We have control and we have the blockade,” Trump said. “Iran is not getting anything. Nothing is going through.”
Iran is badly battered, but has a history of showing resilience
There’s no doubt that the strikes combined with decades of international sanctions have battered Iran, said Aarathi Krishnan, a geopolitical risk analyst at RAKSHA Intelligence Future.

But as Trump tries to turn to a new chapter in the war, Krishnan argues the Republican may be misguided in concluding that more pressure on Tehran — which has spent decades adapting to international economic sanctions — will produce the political outcome he wants.

Indeed, Iran’s economy in the run-up to the start of the war was mired in surging inflation, according to the International Monetary Fund. National income per person had fallen from about $8,000 in 2012 to $5,000 in 2024, according to World Bank data.
But Tehran has also shown resilience, selling discounted oil and establishing opaque shipping and financial networks, Krishnan said.
“This administration has completely underestimated the Iranian resolve,” Krishnan said. “This is not new to the Iranian regime.”
Trump must decide how far he’s willing to go with sanctions

Richard Goldberg, who served as a senior adviser on Iran at the National Security Council during Trump’s first White House term, argues that Iran now finds itself in “uncharted waters” if the administration follows through with a truly biting campaign to pressure Iranian trade partners.

“What we should be seeing is an attempt to seal off every escape hatch the regime has left,” said Goldberg, who is now at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, a hawkish Washington think tank. “Use the economic power of the United States to layer a naval blockade with an air and land embargo while dropping the hammer on anyone who gives the regime access to hard currency — whether that’s in the Middle East, China or even Europe.”
But it remains to be seen how far the administration is willing to go.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent this week unveiled a campaign the White House calls “Operation Economic Outcast,” but only issued warnings to nations to cut trade and has yet to announce any secondary sanctions. Bessent told reporters the administration wanted countries to have a chance to shift away from Iran before it was too late — and acknowledged there was economic risk to the U.S., too, in moving ahead.
China, which is Iran’s biggest trade partner and oil buyer, responded by expressing its opposition to “illegal unilateral sanctions.”
Pressed Thursday about why he wasn’t already sanctioning Chinese banks, Trump offered a cryptic response.
